**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 28, verses 1–6:**

**Explanation of the words:**

**Ṭāsīn Mīm** (طسۤمۤ): This is one of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭa'ah). It is written طسم and read: ṭā, sīn, mīm.

**Tilka** (تلك): That is, the verses composed of letters like these are the verses of the Noble Qur'an.

**Natlū 'alayka** (نتلو عليك): That is, we recite to you, relating to you some of the news of Musa and Fir'awn, that is, some of their story.

**Li-qawmin yu'minūn** (لقوم يؤمنون): That is, for the sake of the believers, so that they may increase in faith and attain certainty in victory and a good outcome.

**'Alā fī al-arḍ** (علا في الأرض): That is, he became arrogant and oppressive. He claimed lordship and oppressed the Children of Israel with a terrible oppression.

**Shī'an** (شيعاً): That is, factions, some of them enemies of others, following the principle of *farriq tasud* (divide and rule).

**Yastaḥyī nisā'ahum** (ويستحي نساءهم): That is, he spared the women and did not slaughter the girls, because he did not fear them, while he slaughtered the boys, fearing for his kingdom from them in the future.

**Wa-nurīdu an namunna** (ونريد أن نمن): That is, we bestow favor upon those who were oppressed, making them leaders and making them the inheritors.

**Mā kānū yaḥdharūn** (ما كانوا يحذرون): That is, from the child who would be born among the Children of Israel and would bring an end to their rule.

**The meanings of the verses:**

**Ṭāsīn Mīm** (﴿طسۤمۤ﴾): The meaning of this utterance is known only to Allah. It has conveyed two great benefits. The first is the inimitability (i'jaz) of the Qur'an, which necessitates belief in it and in the status of the one to whom it was revealed, Muhammad (ﷺ). This Qur'an, which made the Arabs unable to produce a surah like it, is composed of letters like these disjointed letters. This shows that it is the speech and revelation of Allah.

The second benefit is that when the polytheists feared the Qur'an's effect on the hearts of those who heard it, they ordered people to avoid listening to it and used various means to prevent the people of Makkah from hearing it. These letters, because of their strangeness to them, compelled them to listen. When the reciter recited *ṭāsīn mīm*, one of them found himself compelled to listen. When he lent his hearing, the Qur'an penetrated his heart, and he was guided by it, if Allah the Exalted wills guidance for him, as happened to many of them.

Allah's saying, ﴿تِلْكَ آياتُ ٱلْكِتابِ﴾ ("These are the verses of the Book"), means: these are the verses of the Clear Book, that is, the Qur'an which makes clear guidance from error, good from evil, and truth from falsehood. His saying ﴿نَتْلُواْ عَلَيْكَ مِن نَّبَإ مُوسىٰ وفِرْعَوْنَ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾ ("We recite to you, [O Messenger], some of the news of Musa and Fir'awn in truth") means: we recite to you, O Messenger, relating some of the news of Musa and Fir'awn, that is, the account of Musa and Fir'awn.

His saying ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ("for a people who believe") is because they are the ones who benefit from what they hear in their lives, and because they are in a difficult situation in which they need to hear such stories so that they remain steadfast in their faith until Allah grants them victory, as He granted victory to those before them after a weakness greater than their own weakness.

His saying, ﴿إنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ..﴾ ("Indeed, Fir'awn...") to the end of the verse, is an explanation of what He said He would relate to the believers. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿إنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ..﴾ to the end of the verse: indeed Fir'awn, the Egyptian ruler named al-Walid ibn al-Rayyan, the tyrant who claimed lordship and divinity, ﴿عَلا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ ("exalted himself in the land"), that is, in the land of Egypt. The meaning of "exalted" is that he transgressed, became arrogant, and dominated.

His saying ﴿وجَعَلَ أهْلَها﴾ ("and made its people") means: the people of those Egyptian lands ﴿شِيَعاً﴾ ("into factions"), that is, sects, dividing them in order to preserve his kingdom, following the principle of *farriq tasud* (divide and rule), the political doctrine prevailing today in the lands of disbelief and oppression.

His saying ﴿يَسْتَضْعِفُ طَآئِفَةً﴾ ("he oppressed a group") refers to one of those factions, namely the Children of Israel. The manner of their oppression was that he slaughtered their sons at the moment of their birth, ﴿ويَسْتَحْيِي نِساءَهُمْ﴾ ("and spared their women"), that is, their daughters, so that they would grow up for service. The reason for slaughtering the boys was that his soothsayers and political advisers informed him that his kingdom was threatened by the existence of numerous strong Children of Israel in the land. So he adopted a method of reducing their numbers and limiting their increase by slaughtering the male children and sparing the females. This is a policy resembling today's birth control, which is used by the ruined people of today without their realizing it.

His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ كانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾ ("Indeed, he was among the corrupters") is an explanation of the exaltation and tyranny of Fir'awn. It mentions that the cause of that is the blind, unjust policy he practiced, namely that he was ﴿مِنَ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾ ("among the corrupters"), that is, in the land, by committing grave crimes that cannot be described.

His saying, ﴿ونُرِيدُ أن نَّمُنَّ عَلى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتُضْعِفُواْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ ونَجْعَلَهُمْ أئِمَّةً﴾ ("And We wished to bestow favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders"), means: ﴿نَتْلُواْ عَلَيْكَ مِن نَّبَإ مُوسىٰ وفِرْعَوْنَ﴾ ("We recite to you some of the news of Musa and Fir'awn"), that is, some of their account: We wished, that is, We willed, to bestow favor upon those who were oppressed in the land, the land of Egypt, namely the Children of Israel. We bestow favor upon them by their faith and by delivering them from Fir'awn's rule and domination, and We make them leaders in goodness. ﴿ونَجْعَلَهُمُ ٱلْوارِثِينَ﴾ ("and make them the inheritors") of the rule and governance of the lands after the destruction of Fir'awn and his armies. This is the meaning of His saying:

﴿ونُمَكِّنَ لَهُمْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ ("and establish them in the land").

His saying ﴿ونُرِيَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ ("and show Fir'awn") means: among what We relate to you, We wished to show Fir'awn, Haman and their armies, ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ ("from them"), that is, from the Children of Israel, ﴿ما كانوا يحذرونه﴾ ("that which they feared"), namely from the child who would be born among the Children of Israel and would bring an end to Fir'awn's kingdom. This will happen through causes and arrangements that Allah the Exalted will mention, and they are wondrous!

The narrative begins with His saying ﴿وأَوْحَيْنَآ إلىٰ أُمِّ مُوسىٰ..﴾ ("And We revealed to the mother of Musa...") [al-Qasas: 7].

**Lessons (hidaya) of the verses:**

1. Affirmation of the inimitability of the Qur'an, which is a sign that it is truly the Book of Allah.
2. Affirmation of Muhammad's prophethood through this divine revelation.
3. A warning against oppression, domineering over people, and corruption on earth.
4. The believers are the ones who benefit from what is recited to them, for the life of their hearts.
5. Establishing the principle that there is no precaution against divine decree (*lā ḥadhar ma'a al-qadar*).
6. The prohibition of birth control by obliging citizens not to exceed a specified number of children.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 7–11:

Explanation of the words:

*And We revealed to the mother of Musa*: We informed her that she should nurse her son the first nursings that are necessary, then place him in a chest (tabut), then cast him into the river (al-yamm).

*Into the river (al-yamm)*: That is, into the sea, and it is the Nile River.

*And do not fear and do not grieve*: That is, do not fear that he will perish and do not grieve over separation from him; indeed, We will return him to you.

*Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up*: That is, his helpers and men.

*So that he would become for them an enemy and a grief*: That is, in the final outcome of the matter; the lam here is the lam of consequence and eventuality (lam al-'aqibah wa al-sayrurah).

*A comfort of the eye for me and for you*: That is, may my eye and your eye be delighted by him, so that we rejoice and are gladdened.

*And the heart of the mother of Musa became empty*: That is, empty of everything except him, peace be upon him; that is, she thought of nothing except him.

*She was about to disclose him*: That is, she came close to crying out that he was her son and revealing that.

*And she said to his sister, "Follow him"*: That is, follow his trail until you know where he is.

*So she observed him from a distance*: That is, she watched him closely while she was concealed, following him from a far place.

Meaning of the verses:

This is the beginning of the story of Musa with Pharaoh, from his being an infant at the breast until the end of Pharaoh's destruction, over a long span that reached decades. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful⦆, that is, Moses supplicated his Lord, acknowledging his error first, saying: ﴿My Lord⦆, that is, O my Lord, ﴿indeed I have wronged myself⦆, that is, by my killing of the Copt, ﴿so forgive me⦆ this error. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 17–21:

Explanation of the words:

"بما أنعمت علي" (bima an'amta 'alayya): by Your bestowing upon me the forgiveness of my sin.

"فلن أكون ظهيراً للمجرمين" (falan akuna zahiran lil-mujrimin): that is, I will not be a helper to the people of criminality.

"خائفاً يترقب" (kha'ifan yataraqqab): fearful, watching for what will happen, good or otherwise, after the killing.

"استنصره بالأمس" (istansarahu bil-ams): that is, he asked him for help, and he helped him.

"يستصرخه" (yastasrikhuh): that is, he calls on him for help against another Copt.

"إنك لغوي مبين" (innaka laghawiyyun mubin): that is, you are truly one of clear error and manifest misguidance.

"أن يبطش بالذي هو عدو لهما" (an yabtisha bil-ladhi huwa 'aduwwun lahuma): that is, to seize the one who is an enemy of both Musa and the Copt.

"إن تريد إلا أن تكون جباراً" (in turid illa an takuna jabbaran): that is, you only want to be a tyrant who strikes and kills without concern for the consequences.

"من المصلحين" (minal-muslihin): those who make peace among people when they disagree or dispute.

"وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة" (wa ja'a rajulun min aqsal-madina): that is, the believer from the family of Pharaoh, who came from the farthest part of the city.

"إن الملأ يأتمرون بك" (innal-mala'a ya'tamirna bik): that is, they consult together and some of them urge the others to kill you.

"فاخرج إني لك من الناصحين" (fakhruj inni laka minan-nasihin): that is, leave this land for another.

"فخرج منها خائفاً يترقب" (fakharaja minha kha'ifan yataraqqab): fearful of being killed, watching for what will happen to him.

Explanation of the verses:

Earlier in the previous verse it was mentioned that Musa, peace be upon him, had killed a Copt by mistake, that he acknowledged his error to his Lord, the Exalted, and asked His forgiveness, and that God forgave him and let him know of this by whatever means He willed. When Musa knew of God's forgiveness, he pledged that he would not be "a helper to the criminals" in future, and among that is that he would withdraw from Pharaoh and his chiefs, because they are wrongdoers and criminals. So he said:

"﴿Lord, by what You have bestowed upon me﴾": that is, by Your forgiving my error. In view of Your bestowing forgiveness upon me, I pledge to You that "﴿I will never be a helper to the criminals﴾." This is what the verse [17] indicates, namely the first in this context, which is His saying: "﴿He said, 'My Lord, by what You have bestowed upon me, I will never be a helper to the criminals.'﴾" And His saying: "﴿So he became in the city, fearful and watchful﴾": that is, Musa became in the city of Memphis (Munf), the capital of the Pharaonic kingdom, "﴿fearful﴾" of what might follow from his killing of the Copt, "﴿watchful﴾" of events, wondering what they would bring. Then behold, the man who had sought his help the day before, the Israelite who had asked him for help, "﴿cried out to him﴾," that is, called to him at the top of his voice for help. Musa looked at him and approached him to rescue him, saying: "﴿Indeed, you are clearly a misguided one﴾," that is, truly one of manifest error. Misguidance is corruption in conduct and religion, because yesterday you fought and today you are fighting too. "﴿So when he intended to seize﴾," that is, Musa, "﴿the one who was an enemy to both of them﴾," who was the Copt, the Israelite said: "﴿Do you intend to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land﴾," that is, to strike and kill as you wish without fearing the penalty for it. "﴿And you do not want to be among the reformers﴾," who make peace between those who dispute. The Israelite said this because he was a coward and feared Musa's attack, thinking that he meant him, because of what he had said to him: "﴿Indeed, you are clearly a misguided one.﴾"

When the Copt heard what the Israelite had said, he carried it to the palace, for he was one of its agents. The men of the palace gathered under the presidency of Pharaoh, discussing the matter, looking into its circumstances, its outcomes, and what would follow from it. Among the members of this council was the believer of Pharaoh's family, (Hizqil), who was a believer concealing his faith. He came to Musa secretly to inform him of what was being arranged concerning him, and to advise him to leave the country. This is what is stated in His saying, in verse [20] of this context: "﴿And a man came from the farthest part of the city﴾," from its most distant quarter, for the king's palace was at the edge of the city, and it was the city of Pharaoh (Munf). "﴿Hastening﴾," that is, he walked quickly, in earnest, and reached Musa and said: "﴿O Musa, indeed the chiefs are conferring about you to kill you, so leave; indeed I am to you one of the sincere advisers﴾." God, the Exalted, said: "﴿So he left from it﴾," that is, from Pharaoh's lands, "﴿fearful, watching﴾," fearful of being killed, watching for the pursuit and for what would happen to him, whether salvation or otherwise. And he called upon his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, saying:

"﴿My Lord, deliver me from the wrongdoing people﴾": that is, from Pharaoh and his chiefs first, and from every wrongdoer second.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Gratitude for blessings: when God forgave Musa, he thanked Him by pledging never to stand beside a criminal.

2- The evil of keeping company with a foolish, misguided person, for the Israelite's misguidance and folly were what caused Musa's troubles.

3- The obligation to report to the state those who cause corruption and evil in the land, in order to protect it.

4- The duty of giving sincere counsel: the believer of Pharaoh's family knew Musa was free of fault and crime, so it was incumbent upon him to advise Musa to leave the country so that he might be saved, God willing. This was not treachery against the country or the state, because Musa was of the people of perfection, and what happened from him was by way of error; so he supported him and extended his hand to him, rescuing him from certain death.

5- Natural fear is not blameworthy: Musa, peace be upon him, feared, and the fear led him to turn to his Lord in supplication, so He answered him, and to God belongs all praise and grace.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 22–24:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Wa-lammā tawajjaha tilqā' Madyan﴾ (And when he turned towards Madyan): he set his face towards Madyan, which is the city of Shu'ayb.

﴿ʿAsā rabbī an yahdiyanī sawāʾ al-sabīl﴾ (Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right path): I hope my Lord will guide me to the middle of the road, so that I do not go astray and perish. Allah answered him, guided him to the right path, and he reached Madyan.

﴿Wa-lammā warada māʾ Madyan﴾ (And when he arrived at the water of Madyan): he reached a well from which the people of Madyan watered.

﴿Yasqūn﴾ (they water): that is, their livestock of cattle, camels and sheep.

﴿Tadhūdān﴾ (they hold back): that is, they kept their sheep back from the water, so that the place would be clear for them, out of fear of mixing with foreign men without necessity.

﴿Qāla mā khatbukumā﴾ (He said, "What is your matter?"): Moses said to the two women who were holding back, "What is your matter?", that is, what is your situation.

﴿Ḥattā yuṣdira al-riʿāʾ﴾ (until the shepherds depart): "We do not water our flocks until the shepherds have departed and the water is left for us alone."

﴿Thumma tawallā ilā al-ẓill﴾ (Then he turned back to the shade): that is, after he had watered for them, he returned to the shade of the tree under which he had been sitting.

﴿Limā anzalta ilayya min khayr faqīr﴾ (Indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need): that is, of food in which he was in great need, due to the severity of his hunger, peace be upon him.

﴿Tamshī ʿalā istiḥyāʾ﴾ (walking with shyness): that is, placing the edge of her garment over her face out of modesty before him.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues concerning Moses, peace be upon him, after the incident of the killing and the advice to him to leave the land of Egypt for the land of Madyan, the city of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him. Allah, the Exalted, says, informing about him: ﴿And when he turned towards Madyan﴾, that is, when Moses, acting on the advice of the believer from the family of Pharaoh, turned towards Madyan, that is, towards it and its direction, and he had no knowledge of the desert route, and the distance was a journey of eight days. He said: ﴿Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right path﴾, that is, he hoped of his Lord, glorified and exalted, that He would guide him to the straight road so that he would not go astray and perish. Allah answered him, guided him to the road, and he reached the land of Madyan. And His saying in the second verse of this passage [23] ﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan﴾, that is, when he reached the water of Madyan, which is a well from which people water their livestock, ﴿he found upon it﴾, that is, upon the water, ﴿a community of people﴾, that is, a large group watering their animals, ﴿and he found besides them two women﴾, and they were the two daughters of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, ﴿holding back﴾, that is, keeping their flock from mixing with the livestock of the people. He asked them, not out of prying, but their condition prompted him to ask, because he saw the people watering their livestock and departing group after group, while the two women stood over their flock holding it back from the trough so that it would not mix and drink. So he asked them, saying: ﴿What is your matter?﴾, that is, what is your situation? They answered him, saying: ﴿We do not water until the shepherds have departed﴾, because of our weakness and our unwillingness to mix with men, ﴿and our father is an aged old man﴾ who cannot by himself water this livestock, so we water it, but only after the shepherds have departed and water remains in the trough for us to use. When he understood their excuse, he watered their flock for them. ﴿Then he turned back to the shade﴾ under which he had been sitting, which was the shade of a tree, a well-known desert tree called the samur. When he turned back to the shade, he asked his Lord for food, because of the severity of his hunger, for he had left Egypt without provisions or a guide, and were it not for his good opinion of his Lord he would not have set out in this way. So he said: ﴿My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need﴾, that is, food, ﴿in need﴾, that is, in dire need of it.

Within a short time the two daughters reached their father, and he asked them about the reason for their quick return, and they told him. He said to one of them: go to him and say to him, ﴿Indeed my father invites you so that he may reward you for what you watered for us﴾, which is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Then there came to him one of the two women﴾, in answer to Allah's response to him, ﴿walking with shyness﴾, placing the edge of her garment over her face out of modesty. Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said of her that she was not a brazen woman, going out and coming in. The brief message was conveyed as if it were a telegram, and its text is what Allah, the Exalted, has reported in His saying: ﴿Indeed my father invites you so that he may reward you for what you watered for us﴾!! It is also reported that when she was walking before him guiding him to the road, the wind blew and uncovered her legs. Moses said to her: walk behind me and direct me to the road by throwing pebbles toward the way. This is what showed him her trustworthiness, and when she described him to her father as ﴿the strong, the trustworthy﴾, as will come later.

Lessons of the verses:

Among the lessons of the verses:

1- The obligation of good opinion of Allah, the Exalted, strong hope in Him, and reliance upon Him.

2- The virtue of modesty and the honour of believing women who abstain from mixing with men.

3- The manliness of Moses shown in his watering for the two women.

4- The virtue of supplication and of asking Allah, the Exalted, for whatever the servant is in need of.

5- Covering the face before non-mahram men is a practice of believing women from ancient times, and it is not, as the wrongdoers claim, a jahili custom; the two daughters of Shu'ayb grew up in the house of prophethood, purity and chastity, and one of them covered her face from Moses out of modesty and piety.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 22–24:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Wa-lammā tawajjaha tilqā' Madyan﴾ (And when he turned towards Madyan): he set his face towards Madyan, which is the city of Shu'ayb.

﴿ʿAsā rabbī an yahdiyanī sawāʾ al-sabīl﴾ (Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right path): I hope my Lord will guide me to the middle of the road, so that I do not go astray and perish. Allah answered him, guided him to the right path, and he reached Madyan.

﴿Wa-lammā warada māʾ Madyan﴾ (And when he arrived at the water of Madyan): he reached a well from which the people of Madyan watered.

﴿Yasqūn﴾ (they water): that is, their livestock of cattle, camels and sheep.

﴿Tadhūdān﴾ (they hold back): that is, they kept their sheep back from the water, so that the place would be clear for them, out of fear of mixing with foreign men without necessity.

﴿Qāla mā khatbukumā﴾ (He said, "What is your matter?"): Moses said to the two women who were holding back, "What is your matter?", that is, what is your situation.

﴿Ḥattā yuṣdira al-riʿāʾ﴾ (until the shepherds depart): "We do not water our flocks until the shepherds have departed and the water is left for us alone."

﴿Thumma tawallā ilā al-ẓill﴾ (Then he turned back to the shade): that is, after he had watered for them, he returned to the shade of the tree under which he had been sitting.

﴿Limā anzalta ilayya min khayr faqīr﴾ (Indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need): that is, of food in which he was in great need, due to the severity of his hunger, peace be upon him.

﴿Tamshī ʿalā istiḥyāʾ﴾ (walking with shyness): that is, placing the edge of her garment over her face out of modesty before him.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues concerning Moses, peace be upon him, after the incident of the killing and the advice to him to leave the land of Egypt for the land of Madyan, the city of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him. Allah, the Exalted, says, informing about him: ﴿And when he turned towards Madyan﴾, that is, when Moses, acting on the advice of the believer from the family of Pharaoh, turned towards Madyan, that is, towards it and its direction, and he had no knowledge of the desert route, and the distance was a journey of eight days. He said: ﴿Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right path﴾, that is, he hoped of his Lord, glorified and exalted, that He would guide him to the straight road so that he would not go astray and perish. Allah answered him, guided him to the road, and he reached the land of Madyan. And His saying in the second verse of this passage [23] ﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan﴾, that is, when he reached the water of Madyan, which is a well from which people water their livestock, ﴿he found upon it﴾, that is, upon the water, ﴿a community of people﴾, that is, a large group watering their animals, ﴿and he found besides them two women﴾, and they were the two daughters of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, ﴿holding back﴾, that is, keeping their flock from mixing with the livestock of the people. He asked them, not out of prying, but their condition prompted him to ask, because he saw the people watering their livestock and departing group after group, while the two women stood over their flock holding it back from the trough so that it would not mix and drink. So he asked them, saying: ﴿What is your matter?﴾, that is, what is your situation? They answered him, saying: ﴿We do not water until the shepherds have departed﴾, because of our weakness and our unwillingness to mix with men, ﴿and our father is an aged old man﴾ who cannot by himself water this livestock, so we water it, but only after the shepherds have departed and water remains in the trough for us to use. When he understood their excuse, he watered their flock for them. ﴿Then he turned back to the shade﴾ under which he had been sitting, which was the shade of a tree, a well-known desert tree called the samur. When he turned back to the shade, he asked his Lord for food, because of the severity of his hunger, for he had left Egypt without provisions or a guide, and were it not for his good opinion of his Lord he would not have set out in this way. So he said: ﴿My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need﴾, that is, food, ﴿in need﴾, that is, in dire need of it.

Within a short time the two daughters reached their father, and he asked them about the reason for their quick return, and they told him. He said to one of them: go to him and say to him, ﴿Indeed my father invites you so that he may reward you for what you watered for us﴾, which is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Then there came to him one of the two women﴾, in answer to Allah's response to him, ﴿walking with shyness﴾, placing the edge of her garment over her face out of modesty. Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said of her that she was not a brazen woman, going out and coming in. The brief message was conveyed as if it were a telegram, and its text is what Allah, the Exalted, has reported in His saying: ﴿Indeed my father invites you so that he may reward you for what you watered for us﴾!! It is also reported that when she was walking before him guiding him to the road, the wind blew and uncovered her legs. Moses said to her: walk behind me and direct me to the road by throwing pebbles toward the way. This is what showed him her trustworthiness, and when she described him to her father as ﴿the strong, the trustworthy﴾, as will come later.

Lessons of the verses:

Among the lessons of the verses:

1- The obligation of good opinion of Allah, the Exalted, strong hope in Him, and reliance upon Him.

2- The virtue of modesty and the honour of believing women who abstain from mixing with men.

3- The manliness of Moses shown in his watering for the two women.

4- The virtue of supplication and of asking Allah, the Exalted, for whatever the servant is in need of.

5- Covering the face before non-mahram men is a practice of believing women from ancient times, and it is not, as the wrongdoers claim, a jahili custom; the two daughters of Shu'ayb grew up in the house of prophethood, purity and chastity, and one of them covered her face from Moses out of modesty and piety.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verse 25–28:

Explanation of the words:

"And he related to him the stories" (wa qassa ʿalayhi al-qasas): he informed him of his whole matter, from his killing of the Copt, to the seeking of authority against him, to the advice of the believing man to him to leave the land, and his arrival at the water of Madyan.

"Fear not; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people" (lā takhaf najawta min al-qawm al-ẓālimīn): that is, from Pharaoh and his chiefs, for they have no authority over the lands of Madyan.

"O my father, hire him" (yā abati istajirhu): that is, take him as a hired worker to tend our sheep in our stead.

"The strong, the trustworthy" (al-qawiyy al-amīn): his fitness was mentioned to him, which is physical strength and trustworthiness.

"On condition that you hire me" (ʿalā an tajuranī): that is, that you be a hired worker for me in tending my sheep.

"Eight years" (thamāniya ḥijaj): that is, eight years, for a ḥijjah is a year, and its plural is ḥijaj.

"And if you complete ten, it is from you" (fa-in atmamta ʿashran fa-min ʿindika): that is, you made the eight into ten, and you willed the ten; this is from your generosity.

He said, "You will find me, God willing, among the righteous" (qāla satajidunī in shāʾa Allāh mina al-ṣāliḥīn): that is, those who fulfil and do not break or diminish (their covenants).

"That is between me and you" (dhālika bayni wa baynak): I will fulfil my condition, and you will fulfil your condition.

"Whichever of the two terms I fulfil" (ayyamā al-ajalayni qaḍaytu): that is, whether the eight or the ten I complete.

"Then there shall be no transgression against me" (fa-lā ʿudwāna ʿalayy): that is, by seeking an increase beyond the eight or beyond the ten.

"And God is Witness over what we say" (wa Allāhu ʿalā mā naqūlu wakīl): that is, a guardian and watcher; i.e., I call God to witness the contract in both its parts, namely the marriage and the tending of the sheep, and with that the contract was concluded.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with what took place between Moses and the two daughters of Shuʿayb regarding the watering for them, and the coming of one of them to convey to him her father's message, and his walking with her. His words, may He be exalted, ﴿So when he came to him﴾: that is, Moses came to Shuʿayb, ﴿and related to him the stories﴾: that is, he informed him of his whole matter, from his killing of the Copt by mistake, and the seeking of authority against him, and the advice of the believer of Pharaoh's household to him to leave the land, and his arrival at the water of Madyan. Shuʿayb then said to him, ﴿Fear not; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning Pharaoh and his government. This is what is now known as political asylum, so he granted him security for his life, because Pharaoh has no authority over this land.

Shuʿayb said to him: "Sit, and eat with us." Moses said: "I fear that this may be a recompense for what I watered for your two daughters, their flocks; and I am from a household that does not seek a recompense for a good deed." Shuʿayb said to him: "No, this is not a wage for your watering; rather, it is our custom to host the guest and feed the food." So he ate and saw no harm in it.

And His words, may He be exalted, ﴿One of the two said: "O my father, hire him; indeed the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy"﴾. It is related that when she said ﴿indeed the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy﴾, she stirred his wariness with this word, so he asked her: "How did you know that?" She mentioned to him his strength in watering for them, and his trustworthiness in lowering his gaze from looking at her. Shuʿayb believed her, and said to Moses: ﴿Indeed I want to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine﴾, that is, to give you in marriage, ﴿on condition that you hire yourself to me for eight years﴾, that is, years; ḥijjah is a year (al-sanah). His words ﴿And if you complete ten, it is from you﴾: that is, out of your kindness and generosity. ﴿And I do not want to burden you﴾ by requiring the ten. ﴿You will find me, God willing, among the righteous﴾: that is, those who keep their covenants. Moses then replied to his words: ﴿That is between me and you﴾: it is incumbent on me to fulfil what you have stipulated for me, and it is incumbent on you to fulfil what you have stipulated for me on your own part. ﴿Whichever of the two terms I fulfil﴾, the eight or the ten, ﴿I have completed﴾: that is, I have fulfilled and discharged it. ﴿Then there shall be no transgression against me﴾: that is, by seeking an increase beyond the eight, or beyond the ten.

Shuʿayb said: "Yes." ﴿And God is Witness over what we say﴾. So he called God Most High to witness the validity of the contract, and with that Moses became the husband of Shuʿayb's daughter whom he had designated for him, and it is generally held that she was the elder, who had testified to his trustworthiness and strength.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The generosity, nobility and magnanimity of Shuʿayb are manifest in reassuring Moses, honouring him and sheltering him.

2- It is shown that competence is a condition for work, and that nothing is better than strength, which is physical and intellectual capacity, together with trustworthiness.

3- The permissibility of a man offering his daughter to one whom he sees as truthful and trustworthy, so as to marry her to him.

4- The permissibility of calling God to witness contracts, as in ﴿And God is Witness over what we say﴾.

5- The virtue of Moses, peace be upon him, in hiring himself out for the sustenance of his belly and the chastity of his private parts.

It is related that when she said ﴿indeed the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy﴾, she stirred his wariness with this word, so he asked her: "How did you know that?" She mentioned to him his strength in watering for them, and his trustworthiness in lowering his gaze from looking at her. Shuʿayb believed her, and said to Moses: ﴿Indeed I want to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine﴾, that is, to give you in marriage, ﴿on condition that you hire yourself to me for eight years﴾, that is, years; ḥijjah is a year (al-sanah). His words ﴿And if you complete ten, it is from you﴾: that is, out of your kindness and generosity. ﴿And I do not want to burden you﴾ by requiring the ten. ﴿You will find me, God willing, among the righteous﴾: that is, those who keep their covenants. Moses then replied to his words: ﴿That is between me and you﴾: it is incumbent on me to fulfil what you have stipulated for me, and it is incumbent on you to fulfil what you have stipulated for me on your own part. ﴿Whichever of the two terms I fulfil﴾, the eight or the ten, ﴿I have completed﴾: that is, I have fulfilled and discharged it. ﴿Then there shall be no transgression against me﴾: that is, by seeking an increase beyond the eight, or beyond the ten.

Shuʿayb said: "Yes." ﴿And God is Witness over what we say﴾. So he called God Most High to witness the validity of the contract, and with that Moses became the husband of Shuʿayb's daughter whom he had designated for him, and it is generally held that she was the elder, who had testified to his trustworthiness and strength.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The generosity, nobility and magnanimity of Shuʿayb are manifest in reassuring Moses, honouring him and sheltering him.

2- It is shown that competence is a condition for work, and that nothing is better than strength, which is physical and intellectual capacity, together with trustworthiness.

3- The permissibility of a man offering his daughter to one whom he sees as truthful and trustworthy, so as to marry her to him.

4- The permissibility of calling God to witness contracts, as in ﴿And God is Witness over what we say﴾.

5- The virtue of Moses, peace be upon him, in hiring himself out for the sustenance of his belly and the chastity of his private parts.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verse 29–32:

Explanation of the words:

Qada Musa al-ajal (قضى موسى الأجل): He completed the agreed term, which was eight or ten years.

Anasa (آنس): He saw.

Jadhwatun min al-nar (أوجذوة من النار): A thick stick with fire at its head.

La'allakum tasthalun (لعلكم تصطلون): That is, that you may warm yourselves.

Nuda (نودي): That is, Allah the Most High called to him saying, "O Musa, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds."

Fi al-buqʻah al-mubarakah (في البقعة المباركة): The piece of land on which the tree stands, located on the bank of the valley.

Tahtazzu ka'annaha jann (تهتز كأنها جانُّ): It convulsed and moved rapidly, as if it were a snake of the house snakes.

Walla mudbiran wa lam yuʻaqqib (ولى مدبراً ولم يعقب): He turned back fleeing and did not return, out of fear and terror of it.

Usluk yadaka fi jaybika (اسلك يدك في جيبك): Put your hand into the pocket of your garment.

Min ghayr su' (من غير سوء): That is, without a defect such as leprosy or the like.

Wadmum ilayka janahaka min al-rahb (واضمم إليك جناحك من الرهب): Draw your hand to yourself by placing it on your chest, so that your fright may depart.

Fadhanika burhanan (فذانك برهانان): That is, two signs from your Lord confirming the truth of your message.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the story of Musa while he was on his way to Egypt by the arrangement of Allah the Most High. When he had completed the term that he had contracted with his father-in-law Shu'ayb, having fulfilled the better and more complete of the two terms, which was the ten years, he set out walking with his family, his wife and his son, on his way to Egypt to visit his mother and brothers. It happened that he lost his way at night, and it was winter and the cold was severe. Then he perceived "from the side of the mount" (min janib al-Tur), that is, Mount Tur, "a fire" (naran). So he said to his family, "Stay here; indeed I have seen (anastu) a fire," that is, I have perceived a fire, "I will go to it; I will bring you from it some news," since perhaps he would find there someone who would guide us to the way, "or bring you a firebrand from it," that is, a piece of wood with a lit fire at its head, "that you may warm yourselves" (la'allakum tasthalun), that is, so that you may be warmed by it. This is what the verse [29] indicates. And His saying in the second verse, "Then when he came to it" (falamma atahā), that is, came to the fire, "he was called" (nuda), that is, a caller called to him, "from the right side of the valley, in the blessed place, from the tree: O Musa" (an ya Musa), that is, his Lord called him, "O Musa, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds." "And throw down your staff" (wa an alqi 'asaka). So he threw it down, and it convulsed, moved and shook rapidly, "as if it were a jann" (ka'annaha jann), that is, a great snake of the snakes known as janan, "and he turned back fleeing and did not return" (wallā mudbiran wa lam yu'aqqib): that is, he was frightened by it and retreated backward out of fear, "and did not return" (wa lam yu'aqqib), that is, he did not come back to it out of terror. Then his Lord said to him, "Come forward" (aqbil), that is, toward the staff, "and do not fear; indeed you are among the secure" (inaka min al-aminin), that is, those whom their Lord has made secure, so they fear nothing.

And He said to him after he had turned back, "Put your hand into your garment's opening; it will come out white, without any defect" (usluk yadaka fi jaybika takhruj bayda' min ghayr su'). That is, put your hand into the pocket of your garment, which is the slit through which the head passes into the garment when one dons it. His saying "it will come out" (takhruj), that is, the hand, "white" (bayda'), like light, "without any defect" (min ghayr su'), that is, leprosy or the like. "And draw your arm to yourself" (wadmum ilayka janahaka), that is, your hand together with the upper arm to your chest, "from the fear" (min al-rahb), that is, the terror. Then it will depart from you, so that your hand returns to its ordinary state, with no light in it, as it was before you put it into your pocket the first time.

Then He, the Most High, said to him, "These two" (fadhanika), that is, the staff and the white hand, "are two proofs from your Lord" (burhanan min rabbika), that is, two signs indicating your message, by which you are sent to Pharaoh and his chiefs, for they were a people of defiant transgression, going outside the obedience of Allah, in that they disbelieved in Him, worshipped other than Him, and oppressed His servants, so that you may call them to believe in Allah and worship Him, and to send the Children of Israel with you so that you may take them to the Promised Land, that is, Palestine and the surrounding lands of Syria.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Prophets are faithful to their covenants: Musa completed the better and fuller of the two terms, which was the ten years.

2- The permissibility of travelling with one's family; it may happen that a person loses his way or needs something, and he should be patient.

3- The excellence of that blessed place where Allah the Most High spoke to Musa, peace be upon him, which is on Mount Tur.

4- The permissibility of carrying a staff, especially for the traveller and the shepherd or driver of livestock.

5- The permissibility of training in the use of weapons before using them.

6- One is not blamed for natural fear.

7- The sign of the staff and the hand.

8- Whoever is frightened should place his hand on his chest, and his fear will leave, God willing.

9- The condemnation of defiance and its people.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 33–37:

Explanation of the words:

*Inni qataltu minhum nafsan* (إني قتلت منهم نفساً): that is, the soul of the Copt whom he killed by mistake before his migration from Egypt.

*Afsahu minni lisanan* (أفصح مني لساناً): that is, more clear in speech than I.

*Ridan* (ردءاً): that is, a helper for me.

*Sanashuddu 'adudaka bi-akhika* (سنشد عضدك بأخيك): that is, We will support you through him and strengthen you with your brother Harun.

*Wa-naj'alu lakuma sultanan* (ونجعل لكما سلطاناً): that is, a strong proof by which you will have the victory.

*Fa-la yasiluna ilaykum* (فلا يصلون إليكم): that is, [they will not reach you] with harm.

*Bi-ayatina* (بآياتنا): that is, go with Our signs.

*Falamma ja'ahum Musa bi-ayatina* (فلما جاءهم موسى بآياتنا): that is, the staff, the hand, and the other of the nine signs.

*Bayyinat* (بينات): that is, clear.

*Sihrun muftara* (سحر مفترى): that is, fabricated and false.

*Aqibat al-dar* (عاقبة الدار): that is, the praiseworthy end in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 38–43:

Explanation of the words:

"ما علمت لكم من إله غيري" (Ma 'alimtu lakum min ilahin ghayri): That is, a lord who is obeyed, submitted to, and magnified, other than me. May the curse of Allah be upon him; how lying he is.

"يا هامان" (Ya Haman): One of the ministers of Pharaoh, perhaps the minister of industry or of labour and workers.

"فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين" (Fa-awqid li ya Haman 'ala al-tin): That is, bake for me the bricks (ajurr), which is mud baked in fire.

"فاجعل لي صرحاً" (Fa-aj'al li sarhan): That is, a high building, a palace or other.

"لعلي أطلع إلى إله موسى" (La'alli attali'u ila ilahi Musa): That is, that I may stand upon it and look at him.

"وإني لأظنه من الكاذبين" (Wa inni la-azunnuhu min al-kadhibin): That is, Musa in his claim that he has a god other than me.

"فنبذناهم في اليم" (Fa-nabadhnahum fi al-yamm): That is, We cast them into the sea, drowned and destroyed.

"وجعلناهم أئمة" (Wa ja'alnahum a'immatan): That is, leaders who are followed in falsehood.

"يدعون إلى النار" (Yad'una ila al-nar): That is, to disbelief, polytheism, and the sins that necessitate the Fire.

"في هذه الدنيا لعنة" (Fi hadhihi al-dunya la'natan): That is, disgrace and distance from good.

"هم من المقبوحين" (Hum min al-maqbuhin): That is, those removed from every good, whose creation is disfigured.

"القرون الأولى" (Al-qurun al-ula): The people of Noah, the people of Hud, the people of Salih, and others.

"بصائر للناس" (Basa'ir lil-nas): That is, in it is light that guides as sight guides.

Explanation of the verses:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Pharaoh said﴾. When Pharaoh heard the words of Musa, peace be upon him, confirmed by the words of Harun, peace be upon him, and the speech was extremely gentle and affecting, Pharaoh feared defeat. He maneuvered and equivocated, and said to those present: ﴿I know of no god for you other than myself﴾. That is, as Musa claimed; but I will investigate and learn the truth whether there is another god other than me. So he called his minister Haman and ordered him to prepare baked bricks, because he is strong, and to build a high palace reaching the heavens, so that he might search for himself for the god of Musa, if he is as he claims; and indeed I think Musa is lying in his claim that there is a god other than me for him and for you. This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He, in the first verse [38]: ﴿And Pharaoh said, "O chiefs, I know of no god for you other than myself. So kindle for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay and make for me a tower that I may look at the god of Musa, though I think him to be among the liars."﴾ That is, in his claim that there is another god other than me.

His saying: ﴿And he was arrogant, he and his soldiers, in the land﴾, that is, the land of Egypt, ﴿without right﴾ that would entitle them to arrogance, ﴿and they thought that they would not be returned to Us﴾, that is, they denied the Last Resurrection. He said: ﴿So We seized him and his soldiers﴾, that is, because of their arrogance, disbelief, and denial of Allah's signs. ﴿So We cast them into the sea﴾, that is, into the water. He also said to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿So see how was the end of the wrongdoers﴾; indeed it was a burden upon them and a loss for them. His saying: ﴿And We made them leaders who invite to the Fire﴾, that is, We made Pharaoh and his chiefs leaders in disbelief whom the rebellious and tyrants of every time and place follow, ﴿inviting to the Fire﴾ through disbelief, polytheism, and sins, which necessitate the Fire. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped﴾, but their punishment will be doubled, they will be forsaken and humiliated, because whoever calls to an evil practice bears its burden and the burden of those who act upon it, without their burdens being diminished in the least.

His saying: ﴿And We caused a curse to follow them﴾, that is, the family of Pharaoh, ﴿in this world﴾, which ended with them in complete drowning and total loss. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the disfigured﴾, that is, those removed from the mercy of Allah, abiding in Hell, and wretched is the residence of the arrogant. His saying: ﴿And We had certainly given Musa the Scripture﴾, that is, the Torah, after the destruction of the wrongdoers. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Pharaoh said﴾. When Pharaoh heard the words of Musa, peace be upon him, confirmed by the words of Harun, peace be upon him, and the speech was extremely gentle and affecting, Pharaoh feared defeat. He maneuvered and equivocated, and said to those present: ﴿I know of no god for you other than myself﴾. That is, as Musa claimed; but I will investigate and learn the truth whether there is another god other than me. So he called his minister Haman and ordered him to prepare baked bricks, because he is strong, and to build a high palace reaching the heavens, so that he might search for himself for the god of Musa, if he is as he claims; and indeed I think Musa is lying in his claim that there is a god other than me for him and for you. This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He, in the first verse [38]: ﴿And Pharaoh said, "O chiefs, I know of no god for you other than myself. So kindle for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay and make for me a tower that I may look at the god of Musa, though I think him to be among the liars."﴾ That is, in his claim that there is another god other than me.

His saying: ﴿And he was arrogant, he and his soldiers, in the land﴾, that is, the land of Egypt, ﴿without right﴾ that would entitle them to arrogance, ﴿and they thought that they would not be returned to Us﴾, that is, they denied the Last Resurrection. He said: ﴿So We seized him and his soldiers﴾, that is, because of their arrogance, disbelief, and denial of Allah's signs. ﴿So We cast them into the sea﴾, that is, into the water. He also said to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿So see how was the end of the wrongdoers﴾; indeed it was a burden upon them and a loss for them. His saying: ﴿And We made them leaders who invite to the Fire﴾, that is, We made Pharaoh and his chiefs leaders in disbelief whom the rebellious and tyrants of every time and place follow, ﴿inviting to the Fire﴾ through disbelief, polytheism, and sins, which necessitate the Fire. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped﴾, but their punishment will be doubled, they will be forsaken and humiliated, because whoever calls to an evil practice bears its burden and the burden of those who act upon it, without their burdens being diminished in the least.

His saying: ﴿And We caused a curse to follow them﴾, that is, the family of Pharaoh, ﴿in this world﴾, which ended with them in complete drowning and total loss. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the disfigured﴾, that is, those removed from the mercy of Allah, abiding in Hell, and wretched is the residence of the arrogant. His saying: ﴿And We had certainly given Musa the Scripture﴾, that is, the Torah, after the destruction of the wrongdoers. His saying: ﴿after We had destroyed the former generations﴾, that is, the people of Noah, the people of Hud, the people of Salih, and the people of Abraham. His saying: ﴿as evidence﴾, that is, the Book with what it carries of guidance and light. ﴿As evidence﴾, that is, illumination for the people of Israel, by whose light they see everything they need in matters of their religion and their worldly affairs. ﴿And guidance and mercy﴾, that is, clarification for them and mercy for those among them who act by it. His saying: ﴿so that they might remember﴾, that is, the existence of the Book as evidence, guidance, and mercy before them, in a state that calls them always to remember the blessings of Allah upon them, so that they thank Him by believing in Him, His messengers, and obeying Him and obeying His messengers, peace be upon them.

Guidance of the verses:

1- Clarification that Pharaoh had knowledge that he was a servant subject to the Lord, and that Allah is the Lord of the worlds.

2- Affirmation of the attribute of haughtiness and arrogance of Pharaoh, and that he was among the arrogant.

3- Clarification of how the end of the wrongdoers is destruction and corruption.

4- Callers to immorality, obscenity, misguidance, and polytheism are leaders of the people of the Fire, calling to it while they do not perceive.

5- Clarification of Allah's bounty upon the Children of Israel by sending down the Torah among them, a Book entirely of evidence, guidance, and mercy.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 44–47:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa ma kunta bi-janibi al-gharbi* (And you were not on the western side): That is, O our Messenger, you were not present on the western side of Musa (Moses).

*Idh qadayna ila Musa al-amr* (When We decreed to Musa the command): That is, the commission of the message to Pharaoh and his people.

*Wa ma kunta mina al-shahidin* (Nor were you among the witnesses): So that you could know it and report it.

*Wa lakinna ansha'na qurunan fa-tatawala 'alayhimu al-'umur* (But We produced generations, and the life span grew long for them): That is, rather, after Musa We brought into being nations whose lifespans lengthened, so they forgot the covenants, the sciences were effaced, and revelation ceased. Thus We sent you as a Messenger and revealed to you the account of Musa and others.

*Wa ma kunta thawiyan fi ahl Madyan* (Nor were you dwelling among the people of Madyan): That is, O our Messenger, you were not residing among the people of Madyan so as to know their story.

*Wa ma kunta bi-janibi al-Tur idh nadayna* (Nor were you on the side of Mount Tur when We called): That is, you were not beside Mount Tur, which is the Mount of Tur, when We called Musa and revealed to him what We revealed, so that you could report it.

*Ma ataahum min nadhirin min qablika* (No warner had come to them before you): That is, the people of Makkah and the Arabs in general.

*Wa lawla an tusibahum musibah al-kh* (And had it not been that a misfortune would strike them...): That is, so that they would say: "Why not? Had you sent to us a messenger, we would have hastened the punishment upon them, and We would not have sent you to them as a messenger."

Meaning of the verses:

After the conclusion of the stories of Musa with Pharaoh and the sending down of the Torah, "as insights for the people, and guidance and mercy, that they may remember" [al-Qasas: 43], and since the whole narrative was evidence for the prophethood of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), Allah Most High addressed His Messenger, saying: "And you were not" ﴿وما كُنتَ﴾ — that is, present — "on the western side" ﴿بِجانِبِ ٱلْغَرْبِيِّ﴾ — that is, on the western mountain from Musa — "when We decreed to Musa the command" ﴿إذْ قَضَيْنَآ إلىٰ مُوسى ٱلأَمْرَ﴾ — by sending him as a messenger to Pharaoh and his chiefs — "nor were you among the witnesses" ﴿وما كنتَ مِنَ ٱلشّاهِدِينَ﴾ — that is, those present. Then how did you know this and speak of it, unless you are a true messenger?!

His saying: "But We produced generations" ﴿ولَكِنَّآ أنشَأْنا قُرُوناً﴾ — that is, nations after Musa — "so the life span grew long for them" ﴿فَتَطاوَلَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْعُمُرُ﴾ — that is, their lives were prolonged and extended, so they forgot the covenants, the religious sciences were effaced, and revelation ceased. Thus We sent you as a messenger and revealed to you the account of Musa and others. And His saying: "Nor were you dwelling" ﴿وما كُنتَ ثاوِياً﴾ — that is, residing — "among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses" ﴿فِيۤ أهْلِ مَدْيَنَ تَتْلُواْ عَلَيْهِمْ آياتِنا﴾. How then did you know their news, and know that Musa had stayed among them for ten years, unless you were a true messenger to whom the report of the former peoples is revealed? This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: "But We were senders" ﴿ولَكِنّا كُنّا مُرْسِلِينَ﴾ — so We sent you as a messenger and revealed to you the reports of those who passed on.

And His saying: "Nor were you on the side of Mount Tur" ﴿وما كُنْتَ بِجانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ﴾ — that is, the Mount of Tur — "when We called" ﴿إذْ نادَيْنا﴾ Musa and commanded him with what We commanded and informed him of what We informed him. How then did you know that and report it, unless you were a true messenger to whom it is revealed? His exalted saying: "But it was a mercy from your Lord" ﴿ولَٰكِن رَّحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾ — that is, We sent you as a mercy from your Lord to the worlds — "that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you" ﴿لِتُنذِرَ قَوْماً مَّآ أتاهُم مِّن نَّذِيرٍ مِّن قَبْلِكَ﴾ — and they are the people of Makkah and all the Arabs — "that they may remember" ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ — that is, so that they may take heed, believe, be guided, be saved, and be made happy.

And His exalted saying: "And had it not been that a misfortune would strike them" ﴿ولَوْلاۤ أن تُصِيبَهُم مُّصِيبَةٌ﴾ — that is, a punishment — "for what their hands had sent forth" ﴿بِما قَدَّمَتْ أيْدِيهِمْ﴾ — that is, of polytheism and sins — "they would say: Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger" ﴿فَيَقُولُواْ رَبَّنا لَوْلاۤ أرْسَلْتَ إلَيْنا رَسُولاً﴾ — that is, why did You not send us a messenger — "so that we might follow Your verses and be among the believers" ﴿فَنَتَّبِعَ آياتِكَ ونَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾. That is, had it not been for their saying this, We would have hastened the punishment upon them and would not have sent you to them as a messenger. Then what is wrong with them that they do not believe and give thanks?!

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Establishing Muhammadan prophethood by the strongest rational proofs.

2- The mission of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) came at its appointed time, when the need for it was pressing.

3- The Muhammadan mission was a divine mercy by which Allah showed mercy to the worlds.

4- The answer to *Lawla* (had it not been) in His saying "And had it not been that a misfortune would strike them" is omitted; we have mentioned it, and it is: "We would have hastened the punishment upon them and would not have sent you to them as a messenger."

After the conclusion of the stories of Musa with Pharaoh and the sending down of the Torah, "as insights for the people, and guidance and mercy, that they may remember" [al-Qasas: 43], and since the whole narrative was evidence for the prophethood of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), Allah Most High addressed His Messenger, saying: "And you were not" ﴿وما كُنتَ﴾ — that is, present — "on the western side" ﴿بِجانِبِ ٱلْغَرْبِيِّ﴾ — that is, on the western mountain from Musa — "when We decreed to Musa the command" ﴿إذْ قَضَيْنَآ إلىٰ مُوسى ٱلأَمْرَ﴾ — by sending him as a messenger to Pharaoh and his chiefs — "nor were you among the witnesses" ﴿وما كنتَ مِنَ ٱلشّاهِدِينَ﴾ — that is, those present. Then how did you know this and speak of it, unless you are a true messenger?!

His saying: "But We produced generations" ﴿ولَكِنَّآ أنشَأْنا قُرُوناً﴾ — that is, nations after Musa — "so the life span grew long for them" ﴿فَتَطاوَلَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْعُمُرُ﴾ — that is, their lives were prolonged and extended, so they forgot the covenants, the religious sciences were effaced, and revelation ceased. Thus We sent you as a messenger and revealed to you the account of Musa and others. And His saying: "Nor were you dwelling" ﴿وما كُنتَ ثاوِياً﴾ — that is, residing — "among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses" ﴿فِيۤ أهْلِ مَدْيَنَ تَتْلُواْ عَلَيْهِمْ آياتِنا﴾. How then did you know their news, and know that Musa had stayed among them for ten years, unless you were a true messenger to whom the report of the former peoples is revealed? This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: "But We were senders" ﴿ولَكِنّا كُنّا مُرْسِلِينَ﴾ — so We sent you as a messenger and revealed to you the reports of those who passed on.

And His saying: "Nor were you on the side of Mount Tur" ﴿وما كُنْتَ بِجانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ﴾ — that is, the Mount of Tur — "when We called" ﴿إذْ نادَيْنا﴾ Musa and commanded him with what We commanded and informed him of what We informed him. How then did you know that and report it, unless you were a true messenger to whom it is revealed? His exalted saying: "But it was a mercy from your Lord" ﴿ولَٰكِن رَّحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾ — that is, We sent you as a mercy from your Lord to the worlds — "that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you" ﴿لِتُنذِرَ قَوْماً مَّآ أتاهُم مِّن نَّذِيرٍ مِّن قَبْلِكَ﴾ — and they are the people of Makkah and all the Arabs — "that they may remember" ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ — that is, so that they may take heed, believe, be guided, be saved, and be made happy.

And His exalted saying: "And had it not been that a misfortune would strike them" ﴿ولَوْلاۤ أن تُصِيبَهُم مُّصِيبَةٌ﴾ — that is, a punishment — "for what their hands had sent forth" ﴿بِما قَدَّمَتْ أيْدِيهِمْ﴾ — that is, of polytheism and sins — "they would say: Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger" ﴿فَيَقُولُواْ رَبَّنا لَوْلاۤ أرْسَلْتَ إلَيْنا رَسُولاً﴾ — that is, why did You not send us a messenger — "so that we might follow Your verses and be among the believers" ﴿فَنَتَّبِعَ آياتِكَ ونَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾. That is, had it not been for their saying this, We would have hastened the punishment upon them and would not have sent you to them as a messenger. Then what is wrong with them that they do not believe and give thanks?!

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Establishing Muhammadan prophethood by the strongest rational proofs.

2- The mission of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) came at its appointed time, when the need for it was pressing.

3- The Muhammadan mission was a divine mercy by which Allah showed mercy to the worlds.

4- The answer to *Lawla* (had it not been) in His saying "And had it not been that a misfortune would strike them" is omitted; we have mentioned it, and it is: "We would have hastened the punishment upon them and would not have sent you to them as a messenger."

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 48–51:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Then when the truth came to them from Us⦆: that is, Muhammad (ﷺ) as a clear messenger.

They said, "Why was he not given the like of what was given to Musa?": that is, why was he not given the like of what was given to Musa of the miraculous signs, such as the staff and the hand, or a book all at once like the Torah?

"Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Musa before?": that is, how can they demand of you that you be given the like of what was given to Musa when they had disbelieved in what was given to Musa before? When the Jews informed them that they find the description of Muhammad in the Torah, they disbelieved this report and did not accept it.

And they said, "Two kinds of magic, supporting each other": that is, the Torah and the Qur'an are both manifest magic, supporting one another, that is, strengthening each other.

"And if they do not respond to you": that is, by bringing a Book that is more guiding than the Torah and the Qur'an.

"Then know that they only follow their desires": in their disbelief, nothing more, so there is neither intellect nor an illuminating Book.

"And who is more astray than one who follows his desire": that is, none is more astray than him, ever.

"And We have certainly conveyed to them the word, that they might remember": that is, with the reports of the earlier peoples and what We brought down upon them of Our vengeance when they denied Our messengers and rejected Our oneness. ﴿that they might remember﴾: that is, that they might take warning, so they believe and affirm God's oneness.

Explanation of the meaning of the verses:

When the Exalted established the prophethood of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) by proofs stronger and clearer than which there are none, and showed the world's need for them, especially the Arabs, and mentioned that, were it not for their objection, "Why did You not send to us a messenger, so that we would follow Your signs and be among the believers?" (al-Qasas: 47), He would not have sent His messenger to them, He mentions here how the polytheists met that mercy bestowed. He says about them: ﴿Then when the truth came to them from Us⦆, that is, Muhammad the Prophet (ﷺ), they said: ﴿Why was he not given the like of what was given to Musa?⦆, that is, of signs such as the staff and the white hand, so that we would believe in him and affirm his message. The Exalted said: ﴿Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Musa before? They said: "Two kinds of magic, supporting each other."⦆ And they said: ﴿Indeed, we disbelieve in all of them.⦆ This is because when the believers increased and the Quraysh were alarmed by the situation, they sent to the Jews of Medina, asking them, as the people of the earlier Book, about the truth of what Muhammad (ﷺ) was saying. The Jews answered them that they find the attributes of the unlettered Prophet in the Torah, and that he is a true messenger, neither a liar nor a deceiver. The polytheists of the Quraysh thereupon declared their disbelief in the Torah and said: the Torah and the Qur'an are ﴿two kinds of magic⦆ that cooperate, so we do not believe in either, nor in the one who brought them. It was also read as ﴿two magicians⦆, that is, Musa and Muhammad, peace be upon them both, so we do not believe in them.

This is the meaning of the Exalted's words: ﴿Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Musa before? They said: "Two kinds of magic, supporting each other," and they said: "Indeed, we disbelieve in all of them,"⦆ that is, we disbelieve in each of them.

How then are they not ashamed today, demanding of Muhammad that he be given the like of what was given to Musa of signs? How strange! This would bewilder the minds of the polytheists!

As for the Exalted's words: ﴿Say: "Then bring a Book from God that is more guiding than both⦆: that is, say, O Our Messenger, to these polytheists who disbelieved in the Torah and the Qur'an: ﴿Then bring a Book from God⦆ that He sent down with His knowledge, which would be more guiding than the Torah and the Qur'an. ﴿If you are truthful⦆ in your claim that the Criterion and the Torah are two kinds of magic supporting each other.

As for the Exalted's words: ﴿And if they do not respond to you⦆ by bringing a Book from God more guiding than the Criterion and the Torah, and how could they? It is impossible! Then know that in what they say and claim they only follow their desires, and so they have neither intellect nor transmitted text. ﴿And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from God?⦆ O God, indeed none is more astray than him. The result is that none is more astray than these polytheists of the Quraysh. The Exalted's words ﴿Indeed God does not guide the wrongdoing people⦆ are a statement of God's way with the wrongdoers who have multiplied wrongdoing and gone to excess in it, in belief through polytheism and in action through sins; He deprives them of guidance, so they never find guidance.

As for the Exalted's words: ﴿And We have certainly conveyed to them the word, that they might remember⦆: that is, We have conveyed the word to these polytheists of your people, O Our Messenger, namely the reports of those who passed before, and what We brought down upon them of Our might, Our vengeance and Our great punishments when they disbelieved as these disbelieved and denied what these denied. We conveyed to them the word clearly, explained, connected from its beginning to its end, in hope that they would remember, and so be reminded, believe and affirm God's oneness, and thereby be saved from punishment and be shown mercy by entering Paradise.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- A demonstration of the contradiction of the polytheists and of everyone who follows desire and abandons divine guidance.

2- A demonstration of the challenge to the polytheists to bring a Book from God, and of their inability to do so, whereby it became clear that they follow their desires and that none is more astray than them today.

3- A demonstration of God's way of depriving those who go deep into wrongdoing of divine guidance.

4- A demonstration that God, Exalted and Mighty, conveyed the word to the people of Mecca in detail and clarity for their guidance; so to Him belongs praise and favour, and upon the disbelievers is the curse in Hell.

4- A demonstration that God, Exalted and Mighty, conveyed the word to the people of Mecca in detail and clarity for their guidance; so to Him belongs praise and favour, and upon the disbelievers is the curse in Hell.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 52–55:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it⦆: that is, the Torah and the Gospel, which came before the noble Qur'an.

﴿And when it is recited to them⦆: that is, the Qur'an.

﴿Indeed, we were Muslims before it⦆: that is, submitting to Allah, obedient to His command and prohibition.

﴿Their reward twice⦆: that is, their reward is doubled, because they believed in Musa (Moses) and Isa (Jesus) and they believed in Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿And they repel evil with good⦆: that is, they repel evil, whether in speech or in action, with good, whether in speech or in action.

﴿And when they hear vain talk, they turn away from it⦆: that is, idle speech that is not accepted and not approved, because it achieves neither a dirham for livelihood nor a good deed for the Hereafter.

﴿Peace be upon you⦆: this is the greeting of disengagement, meaning they say a word by which they remain safe.

﴿We do not seek the ignorant⦆: that is, we do not seek the company of people of ignorance, because of the harm in it.

Meaning of the verses:

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We have certainly conveyed to them the word⦆ [al-Qasas: 51] also includes the People of the Book, Jews and Christians, since they are like the Arabs in what has been made clear to them of the reports of past generations, the detailed accounts of the destruction of earlier nations, and what was sent down of adversity and punishment upon the deniers. All of them are bound to faith, righteous deeds, and abandoning shirk, disbelief and sins, for salvation and felicity. Here Allah, the Exalted, mentions that a group of the People of the Book believe in the Prophet Muhammad, because he is the truth from their Lord. So Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it⦆ ﴿And when it is recited to them⦆, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿they say: We believe in it; indeed it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before it⦆, that is, before the descent of the Qur'an, ﴿Muslims⦆, that is, monotheists, submitting, worshipping Allah by what He legislated through the tongues of Musa and Isa, peace be upon them both. This verse refers to a group of the People of the Book who believed during the time of the Messenger of Allah and the descent of the Qur'an, among them Abdullah ibn Salam and Salman al-Farisi and others. And the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Those will be given their reward twice⦆, that is, doubled, because they believed in their messenger and acted by what he brought of truth, and they believed in Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought of guidance. And His saying ﴿and they repel⦆, that is, they push back, ﴿with good⦆, which is forgiveness and pardon, ﴿evil⦆, which is harm such as cursing and insult. And His saying ﴿and from what We have provided them, they spend⦆, that is, they give charity from the surplus of their wealth where charity is fitting.

And His saying ﴿And when they hear vain talk, they turn away from it⦆, that is, when those believers from the two People of the Book hear idle talk from foolish people, they turn away from it and do not pay attention to it or to its speaker, and they answer, saying ﴿To us our deeds, and to you your deeds⦆, that is, their results, by which we are recompensed, and by which you are recompensed. ﴿Peace be upon you⦆, that is, leave us alone. We do not seek the friendship of the ignorant, because of the harm and damage that result from the conduct of people who are ignorant of Allah, the Exalted, and of what He loves and dislikes.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Explanation of the excellence of the People of the Book when they believe in the unlettered Prophet and his Book and submit to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

2- The virtue of one who repels evil with good and spends from what Allah has provided him.

3- The virtue of one who turns away from vain talk and from the people of ignorance, and says a word by which he remains safe; this is one of the traits of the servants of the Most Merciful: ﴿And when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace"⦆ [al-Furqan: 63], that is, a word by which they remain safe. And this peace is not a greeting of salutation, but a peace of disengagement.
