Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 56–59:

Explanation of the words:

Innaka la tahdi man ahbabta (إنك لا تهدي من أحببت): i.e., you cannot guide whomever you love, such as Abu Talib, by having him embrace Islam and perfect his Islam.

Wa qalu (وقالوا): i.e., the polytheists of Quraysh.

In nattabi' al-huda ma'aka (إن نتبع الهدى معك): i.e., if we follow you in what you have brought and call to, which is Islam.

Nutakhattaf min ardina (نتخطف من أرضنا): i.e., the tribes of the Arabs will boldly attack us and seize us.

Yujba ilayha thamarat kulli shay' (يجبى إليها ثمرات كل شيء): i.e., the fruits of everything are carried and brought to it from every direction.

Rizqan min ladunna (رزقاً من لدنا): i.e., a provision for you from Us, O people of the Sacred Precinct in Makkah.

Batirat ma'isharatha (بطرت معيشتها): i.e., they denied the blessing of God upon them, so they were extravagant in sins and transgressed in acts of disobedience.

Yab'athu fi ummiha rasulan (يبعث في أمها رسولاً): i.e., in its greatest city, which is the capital.

Illa wa ahluha zalimun (إلا وأهلها ظالمون): by denying the Messenger and persisting in polytheism and disobedience.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like...among the guided﴾. This verse was revealed concerning Abu Talib, the uncle of the Messenger (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) was eager for his Islam because of his previous standing in standing beside the Prophet (ﷺ), protecting and defending him. When his death approached, the Prophet (ﷺ) visited him and presented the two testimonies to him, saying: "O uncle, say 'There is no god but Allah', a word by which I can plead for you before Allah on the Day of Resurrection." Around him were his visitors from the disbelievers of Quraysh and its elders, who forbade him from that, until they said to him: "Do you turn away from the religion of your fathers? Do you turn away from the creed of Abd al-Muttalib, your father?" until he said, "I am upon the creed of Abd al-Muttalib," and died. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I will certainly seek forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from it." Then Allah forbade him, so he did not seek forgiveness for him afterwards. This verse was revealed as consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ), so the Most High said: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like﴾, O our Prophet, ﴿but Allah guides whom He wills﴾, for He knows that he seeks guidance and does not turn away from it as Abu Talib turned away, and Abu Lahab and others, ﴿and He is most knowing of the guided﴾, i.e., of those who, in His knowledge, are destined to be guided.

The words of the Most High: ﴿If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched from our land﴾. This is an excuse offered by some of the leaders of Quraysh, who said: "We know that what you have brought is true, but we fear that if we believe in you and follow you, the Arabs will unite against us and attack us with one bow, and we will become prey for raiders, as has happened to others. Thus we would be deprived of this security and prosperity, and our conditions would deteriorate. Therefore we excuse ourselves from following you in what you have brought and what you call to, namely disbelief in our gods, destroying them and abandoning them." The Most High responded to this weak and frigid excuse: ﴿Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary, to which the fruits of all things are brought as a provision from Us?﴾ i.e., We did not make for them a land of a sanctuary that We have made inviolable, where no blood is shed, no game is hunted, and no one is seized within it for any offence. Is this not sufficient for them to know that He who made for them a secure sanctuary is able to secure them if they believe and submit, and all the more so?

﴿But most of them do not know﴾: this is the cause of their persistence in polytheism and disbelief. It is ignorance of Allah, His greatness, His knowledge and His wisdom. The meaning of "yujba" or "tujba ilayhi thamarat kulli shay'" is that it is carried to it and driven to it from all regions of the land the fruits of everything, from all kinds of provisions; and this was a provision from Him, the Most High, for the people of the Sacred Precinct. ﴿Will they not then be grateful?﴾

The words of the Most High: ﴿And how many a city We destroyed﴾, i.e., and many people of towns We destroyed, ﴿which exulted in its livelihood﴾, because they became insolent regarding their living, did not thank Allah for His blessing upon them, and were extravagant in wrongdoing and disobedience, so We destroyed them. ﴿And those are their dwellings﴾, i.e., their homes, ﴿which were not inhabited after them except a little﴾, like the dwellings of 'Ad, Thamud and the overturned cities. ﴿And We are the inheritors﴾ of them, so We did not bequeath them to others, and We left them desolate and empty, uninhabited. Will they not consider this, so that they know by it Our power, and so they fear Us, rely upon Us, believe, affirm divine unity, and remain steadfast upon the path of truth which you, O Our Messenger, have brought?

The words of the Most High: ﴿And your Lord would never destroy the cities﴾, O Messenger, ﴿until He had sent into their mother [city] a messenger﴾, as He sent you into the mother of cities, Makkah, ﴿reciting to them Our verses﴾. I.e., this is not the custom of Allah; rather He does not destroy a nation until He sends into the mother city of its lands a messenger reciting to them the verses of Allah that make clear truth from falsehood, good from evil. The consequence of this is the words of the Most High: ﴿And We would never destroy the cities unless their people were wrongdoers﴾, i.e., it was not the custom of Allah, in His worship, to destroy the cities except after their people had committed wrongdoing.

Thus destruction has two conditions:

First: that a messenger be sent who recites His signs, and they deny him and disbelieve in him and in what he brought.

Second: that the people of the cities wrong and transgress, by manifesting falsehood and wrongdoing, spreading evil and corruption in the lands. This is from the justice of Allah and His mercy toward His servants; indeed He is more merciful to them than they are to themselves, and how could it not be, when among His names and attributes are the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Establishing the principle that there is no guide except Allah. The guidance that is negated is the illumination of the servant's heart and the granting of success to the servant to believe, do righteous deeds, and abandon polytheism and disobedience. The guidance that is affirmed, as the Most High says, "And indeed, you guide to a straight path" (42:52), is the guidance of calling, admonition and direction, and of it is the verse "And for every people there is a guide" (13:7), i.e., one who calls them to guidance.

2- Manifestations of Allah's power, knowledge, mercy and wisdom in what He placed in the hearts of the ignorant polytheist Arabs of reverence for the Sacred Precinct and its people, to prepare for its inhabitants security and livelihood, as the Most High says, "So let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and secured them against fear" (106:3–4).

3- From Allah's mercy and justice is that He does not destroy any nation unless two conditions for its destruction are fulfilled:

1- that He sends among them a messenger reciting to them the signs of Allah, which carry guidance and light;

2- that its people wrong themselves by denying the messenger, disbelieving in what he brought, and persisting in disbelief and disobedience.

4- History repeats itself, as they say. What the polytheists offered as an excuse for refusing to accept Islam, on the pretext of the Arabs uniting against them and the disruption of their trade, is offered today by many officials, who have suspended the legal punishments, submitted to the West in separating religion from the state, and permitted grave sins such as usury, drinking alcohol and abandoning prayer, lest they be called backward and rigid; so the West withholds aid from them and besieges them economically.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 60–61:

Explanation of the words:

"And whatever you have been given of a thing": that is, whatever wealth or goods Allah has given you.

"Then it is the enjoyment of the worldly life and its adornment": that is, it is what you enjoy and adorn yourselves with, and then it vanishes and perishes.

"And what is with Allah is better and more lasting": that is, what is with Allah of reward, which is Paradise, is better and more lasting.

"Will you not then use reason?": because one who prefers the little that perishes over the abundant that endures has no reason.

"A good promise": that is, Paradise.

"Then he is one to meet it": that is, one who will attain it, obtain it, and triumph in it without doubt.

"Among those brought forth": that is, into the fire of Hell.

The meaning of the two verses:

The polytheists had earlier, in this context, excused themselves from Islam with a purely material excuse, namely the existence of enmity between them and the rest of the Arabs, which entails wars, disruption of trade, and so on. So His saying here, ﴿And whatever you have been given of a thing – then it is the enjoyment of the worldly life and its adornment﴾, is addressed to them and to everyone who prefers the life of this world over the Hereafter, so that they make lawful what is forbidden, neglect the rulings, and waste the obligations and duties, because these seem to them to conflict with gathering wealth and enjoying worldly life. His saying: ﴿And whatever you have been given of a thing﴾ means: of wealth and goods, however much it may be. ﴿Then it is the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾ means: it is the enjoyment of the worldly life, ﴿and its adornment﴾, which you enjoy and adorn yourselves with for days or years, and then it is spent and vanishes, or you die and leave it behind. ﴿And what is with Allah﴾ of the bliss of Paradise ﴿is better and more lasting﴾: better in its kind and more lasting in its duration. The first is inferior, accompanied by troubles and followed by turbidity, while the second is good, wholesome, free from troubles and turbidities, and enduring, not decaying, not vanishing, and its possessor neither dies nor leaves it behind. ﴿Will you not then use reason?﴾ O you who prefer the perishing over the enduring, the inferior over the good, and the evil over the good. His saying: ﴿Is one to whom We have promised a good promise﴾, and he is the believer, true in his faith, confirmed by his righteous deeds, ﴿to whom We have promised a good promise﴾, which is Paradise, the abode of peace, ﴿then he is one to meet it﴾: that is, he will meet his promise by Allah's permission as soon as he breathes his last and his soul ascends to the heaven. ﴿Like one whom We have given enjoyment of the worldly life﴾, so he eats, drinks and mates like the beasts, ﴿then on the Day of Resurrection he is among those brought forth﴾ into Hell, in the abode of punishment and humiliation. The answer: the two are never equal, and how far apart they are. The first, the righteous believer promised the abode of peace, cannot be compared with the disbeliever who is absorbed in the world, then leaves it suddenly and finds himself with the people of disbelief and crime, in a punishment and humiliation that never leaves him and from which he never emerges.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The benefit of reason is that its possessor restrains himself from what harms him and drives him toward what benefits him. If it does not restrain him from what harms him and does not drive him toward what benefits him, then it does not truly exist, and its existence is like its non-existence.

2- Explanation of the excellence of the Hereafter over this world.

3- Allah's promise to the believer of Paradise is better than what the disbeliever is given of wealth, goods and adornment in the life of this world.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 62–67:

Explanation of the words:

"And the day He calls to them": that is, the Lord, glorified and exalted.

"You used to claim": that is, that they were partners to Me, so you worshipped them alongside Me.

"The word has become due against them": that is, the punishment of the Fire, and they are the leaders of misguidance.

"We led them astray": that is, they went astray, and We did not compel them into error.

"We disown before You": that is, they did not worship us; rather, they worshipped their own desires.

"And it will be said, 'Call upon your partners'": that is, call upon them so that they may deliver you from what you are in.

"If only they had been guided": that is, when they saw the punishment, they wished that they had been among the guided in the world.

"And the day He calls to them": that is, Allah, blessed and exalted.

"The reports will be obscured to them": that is, the reports by which they could have argued became hidden from them.

"So they will not question one another": that is, they will be cut off from speech.

"As for one who repents and believes": that is, believes in Allah and His Messenger and repents from shirk.

"And does righteous deeds": he performs the obligatory duties and required acts.

Yakhluqu ma yashaʾ (He creates whatever He wills): that is, from His creation.

Wa yakhtar (and chooses): that is, whom He wills for prophethood and obedience.

Ma kana lahum (It is not for them): that is, for the polytheists.

Al-khiyara (choice): that is, choosing in anything.

Subhan Allah (Glory be to Allah): that is, exalting Allah above shirk.

Ya'lamu ma tukinnu sudooruhum (He knows what their breasts conceal): that is, what they hide and keep secret of disbelief and other things.

Lahu al-hamd fi al-ula (To Him belongs praise in the first life): that is, in this world, for He is the master of every blessing.

Wa fi al-akhirah (and in the Hereafter): that is, in Paradise.

Wa lahu al-hukm (And to Him belongs judgment): that is, the binding decree.

Wa ilayhi turja'un (And to Him you will be returned): after resurrection, and that is the Day of Resurrection.

Meaning of the verses:

Earlier verses before these condemned shirk, rebuked the polytheists, and challenged them to call upon their associates to deliver them from the humiliation and punishment they were in. Their shirk was by their own choice and free will, since those they had chosen as gods besides Allah disowned them, and they worshipped them alongside Allah. In this verse, Allah exposes their error in choosing, and this is on two counts. The first is that they have no right to choose. For the One who creates creatures is the one who chooses from among them whom He wills for prophethood or obedience. But one who is created and does not create, how can choice be valid from him? The second is that, by the fact that they are created and nurtured by Allah, and they know this, for if anyone asked them, "Who created you?" they would say, "Allah," it was incumbent upon them and required of them to ask Allah, their Creator, to choose for them what they should worship and to explain to them how they should worship, since He is their true Master and they have no master other than Him. But to be headstrong and choose for themselves what they worship is a great wrong, for which they deserve blame in this world and punishment in the Hereafter. Allah says:

[68] ﴿And your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses.﴾ That is, and your Lord, O Muhammad, creates whatever He wills of those He wishes to create, and chooses whom He wills for what He wills, from among whomever He wills of His servants, for what He wills of perfection or deficiency. As for His servants, they have no right of choice; rather, they must hear and obey. Allah says: ﴿It is not for them to choose﴾ that is, the right of choice; rather, what Allah chooses is what the servant must choose. The Prophet ﷺ used to supplicate and say: "O Allah, choose for me and grant me good choice," and he taught his Companions the supplication of istikhara (seeking goodness through choice) just as he taught them a surah of the Qur'an, and he urged them to seek guidance in a matter seven times. And His saying: ﴿Glory be to Allah, and exalted is He above what they associate﴾ exalts Himself above the shirk of the polytheists and the falsehood of the falsifiers. And His saying: ﴿And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they reveal﴾ is evidence that choice belongs to Him alone and not to anyone else, for the One who knows the outward and inward, the beginnings and the ends, before the start and the finish, is the One who chooses. As for one who does not know what his brother conceals in his breast, nor even what another beside him reveals, that is, does not know its outcome, how can choice be valid from him, or how can he have choice in anything?

Moreover, He, may He be glorified and exalted, is Allah, there is no god but He, that is, the worshipped one with no true worship but His, to whom belongs praise in this world, since everything in this world is His creation, His grace, and His bounty, and to whom belongs praise in the Hereafter, when the people of Paradise praise Him, saying, "Praise be to Allah who has removed grief from us" (Qur'an 35:34), and the life of this world is like the Hereafter, concluding with praise to Allah. Allah says: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [al-Zumar: 75] ﴿And to Him belongs judgment, and to Him you will be returned﴾ that is, and to Him belongs judgment, that is, the decree, in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾: just as judgment belongs exclusively to Him, so too does return to Him, and on the day they return to Him, He will judge among them by His judgment, and He is the Mighty, the All-Knowing.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Establishing the principle: "It is not the servant's right to choose except what Allah has chosen for him."

2- The obligation to seek choice in all matters from Allah, by the servant's saying, "O Allah, choose for me and grant me good choice."

3- Affirmation of the sunnah of istikhara, which is: when the servant resolves upon a matter, he prays two rak'ahs at a time when voluntary prayer is not disliked, then supplicates with the supplication of istikhara as narrated in the Sahih: "O Allah, I seek Your guidance by Your knowledge, and seek ability by Your power, and I ask You of Your great bounty, for You are able and I am not able, You know and I do not know, and You are the Knower of the unseen. O Allah, if You know that this matter is good for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affairs, then decree it for me, make it easy for me, and then bless me in it. O Allah, if You know that this matter is bad for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affairs, then turn it away from me and turn me away from it, and decree for me what is good wherever it may be, and make me content with it." He names the need he resolved upon, whether a journey, marriage, construction, trade, or planting.

4- Affirmation of Tawhid and refutation of polytheistic rivalry (tandid, setting up equals).

5- The obligation to praise and thank Allah in every state, because blessings are renewed at every moment.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 71–75:

Explanation of the words:

ارأيتم (ara'aytum): i.e., tell me.

سرمداً (sarmadan): i.e., perpetually, a single unbroken night not followed by day.

بضياء (bi-diya'): i.e., a light like the light of day.

بليل تسكنون فيه (bi-layli taskununa fihi): i.e., you sleep, so your limbs rest and you are relieved of the fatigue of life.

لتسكنوا فيه (li-taskunu fihi): i.e., in the night.

ولتبتغوا من فضله (wa-li-tabtaghu min fadlihi): i.e., that you seek provision from the bounty of God during the day.

ولعلكم تشكرون (wa-la'allakum tashkurun): i.e., so that you thank your Lord by obeying Him, such as through prayer, fasting and charity.

ونزعنا من كل أمة شهيداً (wa-naza'na min kulli ummatin shahidan): i.e., We brought forth from every nation one who bears witness against it, and he is its prophet, peace be upon him.

فقلنا هاتوا برهانكم (fa-qulna hatu burhanakum): i.e., your proofs for the validity of the polytheism about whose consequences Our messengers warned you, but you accepted neither the warning nor the good news.

فعلموا أن الحق لله (fa-'alimu anna al-haqqa lillah): i.e., it became clear to them that worship and the true religion belong to God alone, not to anyone else.

وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون (wa-dalla 'anhum ma kanu yaftarun): i.e., what they used to fabricate of false statements, with which they opposed the messengers, peace be upon them, was lost to them.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to establish monotheism and refute the setting up of rivals to God among His creatures. God said to His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ: Say to these polytheists who have set up rivals to God, though He is their Creator, their Provider and the one who manages the affairs of their lives: ﴿Tell me﴾, i.e., inform me, ﴿if God made the night perpetual for you until the Day of Resurrection﴾, i.e., continuous, one unbroken night not followed by day. ﴿Is there any god other than God who could bring you light?﴾ like the light of day. The answer is: no one. So how can you associate idols with Him? ﴿Will you not then listen?﴾ to what is said to you. And say to them also: ﴿Tell me, if God made the day perpetual for you﴾, i.e., continuous, never followed by night, ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾, until this universe comes to an end, this life ends, and people stand before their Lord from their graves on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Who is the god other than God who could bring you a night in which you rest?﴾ in which you repose in sleep, stillness and not moving. If you say that no one can bring you a night in which to rest, then why do you not perceive these signs, and why do you not hear the proofs and decisive arguments they carry, which establish that there is no god but God and no one worthy of worship besides Him? God's words: ﴿And from His mercy He made for you the night and the day﴾, since it was not obligatory upon Him, but is rather a bounty and mercy from Him. So the night is for you to rest in, and the day is for you to move about and seek your provision from God's bounty; and thereby you are prepared to give thanks: when you eat, drink, ride or dismount, you say, "Praise be to God," and praise of God is the head of thanks. Likewise, night and day are the times for worship, which is thanks, for acts of worship take place only in night and day: fasting in the day, standing in prayer by night, and prayer and charity in both. God's words: ﴿And the day He calls them﴾, i.e., remember, O Messenger, for their instruction and admonition, the day on which the Lord, blessed and exalted, calls to them and says: ﴿Where are My partners whom you used to claim?﴾ that they were My partners, so you worshipped them. Is it hoped that they will answer? No, no. This question and its like is a question of rebuke, reproach and censure, and it is a kind of psychological punishment, which is more severe than physical punishment.

God's words: ﴿And We will draw forth from every nation a witness﴾, i.e., and remember for them this scene from the difficult scenes of the Resurrection. ﴿We will draw forth﴾, i.e., We will bring forth, ﴿from every nation a witness﴾ who testifies against it, and he is its prophet. The Messenger will testify that he conveyed, advised and warned. And it will be said to them: ﴿Bring your proof﴾ for the validity of what you used to worship and call upon. God said: ﴿Then they will know that the truth belongs to God﴾, i.e., it will become clear to them that the truth belongs to God, meaning the true religion belongs to God. He alone deserves to be deified by those who deify, obeyed by the obedient, and approached by those who draw near; there is no god besides Him and no lord other than Him.

Guidance from the verses:

1- A scientific indication that hearing occurs with stillness and little clamour, and that seeing occurs with light, and is not complete in darkness under any circumstances.

2- A strong demonstration of the obligation to affirm God's oneness, since no lord other than Him governs the universe.

3- That the day and night being times for rest and for seeking a livelihood are from God's mercy, a matter that requires thanking God by praising Him, acknowledging His blessing, and obeying Him by spending the blessing on what pleases Him and does not displease Him.

4- An explanation of the horrors of the Resurrection, by mentioning some of its difficult scenes.

5- When the Day of Resurrection comes, every falsehood and false speech will be nullified, and only the word of truth and sincerity will remain.

سرمداً (sarmadan): i.e., perpetually, a single unbroken night not followed by day.

بضياء (bi-diya'): i.e., a light like the light of day.

بليل تسكنون فيه (bi-layli taskununa fihi): i.e., you sleep, so your limbs rest and you are relieved of the fatigue of life.

لتسكنوا فيه (li-taskunu fihi): i.e., in the night.

ولتبتغوا من فضله (wa-li-tabtaghu min fadlihi): i.e., that you seek provision from the bounty of God during the day.

ولعلكم تشكرون (wa-la'allakum tashkurun): i.e., so that you thank your Lord by obeying Him, such as through prayer, fasting and charity.

ونزعنا من كل أمة شهيداً (wa-naza'na min kulli ummatin shahidan): i.e., We brought forth from every nation one who bears witness against it, and he is its prophet, peace be upon him.

فقلنا هاتوا برهانكم (fa-qulna hatu burhanakum): i.e., your proofs for the validity of the polytheism about whose consequences Our messengers warned you, but you accepted neither the warning nor the good news.

فعلموا أن الحق لله (fa-'alimu anna al-haqqa lillah): i.e., it became clear to them that worship and the true religion belong to God alone, not to anyone else.

وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون (wa-dalla 'anhum ma kanu yaftarun): i.e., what they used to fabricate of false statements, with which they opposed the messengers, peace be upon them, was lost to them.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to establish monotheism and refute the setting up of rivals to God among His creatures. God said to His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ: Say to these polytheists who have set up rivals to God, though He is their Creator, their Provider and the one who manages the affairs of their lives: ﴿Tell me﴾, i.e., inform me, ﴿if God made the night perpetual for you until the Day of Resurrection﴾, i.e., continuous, one unbroken night not followed by day. ﴿Is there any god other than God who could bring you light?﴾ like the light of day. The answer is: no one. So how can you associate idols with Him? ﴿Will you not then listen?﴾ to what is said to you. And say to them also: ﴿Tell me, if God made the day perpetual for you﴾, i.e., continuous, never followed by night, ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾, until this universe comes to an end, this life ends, and people stand before their Lord from their graves on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Who is the god other than God who could bring you a night in which you rest?﴾ in which you repose in sleep, stillness and not moving. If you say that no one can bring you a night in which to rest, then why do you not perceive these signs, and why do you not hear the proofs and decisive arguments they carry, which establish that there is no god but God and no one worthy of worship besides Him? God's words: ﴿And from His mercy He made for you the night and the day﴾, since it was not obligatory upon Him, but is rather a bounty and mercy from Him. So the night is for you to rest in, and the day is for you to move about and seek your provision from God's bounty; and thereby you are prepared to give thanks: when you eat, drink, ride or dismount, you say, "Praise be to God," and praise of God is the head of thanks. Likewise, night and day are the times for worship, which is thanks, for acts of worship take place only in night and day: fasting in the day, standing in prayer by night, and prayer and charity in both. God's words: ﴿And the day He calls them﴾, i.e., remember, O Messenger, for their instruction and admonition, the day on which the Lord, blessed and exalted, calls to them and says: ﴿Where are My partners whom you used to claim?﴾ that they were My partners, so you worshipped them. Is it hoped that they will answer? No, no. This question and its like is a question of rebuke, reproach and censure, and it is a kind of psychological punishment, which is more severe than physical punishment.

God's words: ﴿And We will draw forth from every nation a witness﴾, i.e., and remember for them this scene from the difficult scenes of the Resurrection. ﴿We will draw forth﴾, i.e., We will bring forth, ﴿from every nation a witness﴾ who testifies against it, and he is its prophet. The Messenger will testify that he conveyed, advised and warned. And it will be said to them: ﴿Bring your proof﴾ for the validity of what you used to worship and call upon. God said: ﴿Then they will know that the truth belongs to God﴾, i.e., it will become clear to them that the truth belongs to God, meaning the true religion belongs to God. He alone deserves to be deified by those who deify, obeyed by the obedient, and approached by those who draw near; there is no god besides Him and no lord other than Him.

Guidance from the verses:

1- A scientific indication that hearing occurs with stillness and little clamour, and that seeing occurs with light, and is not complete in darkness under any circumstances.

2- A strong demonstration of the obligation to affirm God's oneness, since no lord other than Him governs the universe.

3- That the day and night being times for rest and for seeking a livelihood are from God's mercy, a matter that requires thanking God by praising Him, acknowledging His blessing, and obeying Him by spending the blessing on what pleases Him and does not displease Him.

4- An explanation of the horrors of the Resurrection, by mentioning some of its difficult scenes.

5- When the Day of Resurrection comes, every falsehood and false speech will be nullified, and only the word of truth and sincerity will remain.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 76–78:

Explanation of the words:

"Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Musa": that is, a cousin of Musa, peace be upon him.

"And he oppressed them": that is, he wronged them and acted arrogantly towards them.

"Indeed, its keys would burden a group of strong men": that is, Allah had given him so much wealth that its keys were too heavy for a band (ʿusbah, a group) of men to carry.

"Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not like the exultant": that is, do not exult with the exultation of insolence and haughtiness.

"And seek, through what Allah has given you, the Hereafter": that is, seek, through the wealth you have been given, the Hereafter by doing good deeds.

"I was given it only on knowledge I have": that is, on Allah's knowledge that I deserve it.

"And greater in accumulation": that is, of wealth.

"And the criminals will not be asked about their sins": that is, because Allah knows about them, so they will enter the Fire without reckoning.

Meaning of the verses:

This begins the account of Qarun the rebel. He was Qarun son of Yashhar son of Qahath son of Lawi son of Yaʿqub son of Ishaq son of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. He was a cousin of Musa son of ʿImran and also his maternal cousin, and he was called "al-Munawwar" (the Illuminated) for the beauty of his appearance. He acted hypocritically, as the cast-out Samiri did. Allah the Exalted said, mentioning his account: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Musa﴾, that is, an Israelite, a cousin of Musa son of ʿImran the Messenger. ﴿And he oppressed them﴾, that is, he wronged the Children of Israel and tyrannised over them. It may be that Pharaoh had appointed him as a commander over the Children of Israel, and it made him arrogant, and he amassed great wealth, which made him proud and heedless. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We gave him of the treasures such that its keys would burden a group of strong men﴾. This divine report is evidence of the great wealth that the tyrant Qarun possessed, such that its keys would weigh heavily upon a band (ʿusbah), that is, a group of men, even if they all carried them, because of their weight. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿When his people said to him﴾, that is, the Israelites, admonishing and reminding him, ﴿Do not exult﴾, that is, over your wealth, with the exultation of the insolent and the haughty, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not like the exultant﴾, that is, the insolent and haughty who strut, boast and act proudly. ﴿And seek﴾, that is, seek ﴿through what Allah has given you﴾ of wealth ﴿the Abode of the Hereafter﴾, by giving charity from it and spending in the way of Allah, such as building a mosque, a school, an orphanage, a shelter, or other forms of righteousness and kindness. ﴿And do not forget your share of the world﴾, so eat, drink, dress, ride and dwell, but without extravagance or arrogance. ﴿And do good﴾ in the worship and obedience of Allah the Exalted and do good to His servants by word and deed, ﴿as Allah has done good to you﴾, that is, as Allah the Exalted has done good to you. ﴿And seek not corruption in the land﴾ by abandoning the obligations and committing the prohibitions. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not like the corrupters﴾. Whoever Allah does not love, He hates, and whoever He hates, He punishes in this world and the Hereafter. After this admonition from his righteous people, the people of knowledge and insight, this tyrant Qarun rejected it with what Allah the Exalted reported of him in His saying in verse [78]: ﴿He said: I was given it only on knowledge I have with me﴾, that is, do not threaten me or frighten me with the removal of my wealth from me if I do not do good. For this wealth, ﴿I was given it﴾, that is, Allah gave it to me with knowledge of me that I deserve it, and therefore He gave me and increased my giving. Allah the Exalted answered him in his claim: ﴿Does he not know﴾, that is, does he say what he says of this false claim without knowing ﴿that Allah had destroyed before him generations that were greater than him in strength and greater in accumulation﴾, such as ʿAd, Thamud and the people of Ibrahim. For if abundance of wealth were evidence of Allah's love and His approval of its possessor, He would not have destroyed ʿAd, Thamud and the people of Nuh before him, though they were stronger, and had more wealth and men. And His saying the Exalted: ﴿And the criminals will not be asked about their sins﴾, that is, when a servant greatly commits crimes through shirk and disobedience, the word of punishment becomes binding upon him and the time of his punishment arrives, and he will not be asked about his sins; rather he will be seized suddenly, just as these criminals will enter the Fire without reckoning, so they will not be questioned nor called to account.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks, and they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾ [al-Rahman: 41], that is, they will be thrown into Hell, and it will be said to them: ﴿This is Hell, which the criminals used to deny﴾ [al-Rahman: 43].

Guidance of the verses:

1- Wealth and high position are a means of corrupting a person, except for those whom Allah the Mighty and Majestic has mercy upon, and they are few.

2- The exultation in wealth and authority is forbidden when it is exultation of insolence, pride, self-glorification, arrogance and vanity.

3- Among Allah's favours upon the community is that there exist within it scholars who advise, guide and direct.

4- It is part of prudence for a person to seek from wealth, standing and position the highest ranks in Paradise.

5- Eating of the good, drinking of the good, and dressing, riding and dwelling are permissible, without extravagance, vanity or arrogance.

6- Whoever is blessed with health, wealth and the might of rulership is afflicted with delusion, except those whom Allah has mercy upon.

"Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not like the exultant": that is, do not exult with the exultation of insolence and haughtiness.

"And seek, through what Allah has given you, the Hereafter": that is, seek, through the wealth you have been given, the Hereafter by doing good deeds.

"I was given it only on knowledge I have": that is, on Allah's knowledge that I deserve it.

"And greater in accumulation": that is, of wealth.

"And the criminals will not be asked about their sins": that is, because Allah knows about them, so they will enter the Fire without reckoning.

Meaning of the verses:

This begins the account of Qarun the rebel. He was Qarun son of Yashhar son of Qahath son of Lawi son of Yaʿqub son of Ishaq son of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. He was a cousin of Musa son of ʿImran and also his maternal cousin, and he was called "al-Munawwar" (the Illuminated) for the beauty of his appearance. He acted hypocritically, as the cast-out Samiri did. Allah the Exalted said, mentioning his account: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Musa﴾, that is, an Israelite, a cousin of Musa son of ʿImran the Messenger. ﴿And he oppressed them﴾, that is, he wronged the Children of Israel and tyrannised over them. It may be that Pharaoh had appointed him as a commander over the Children of Israel, and it made him arrogant, and he amassed great wealth, which made him proud and heedless. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We gave him of the treasures such that its keys would burden a group of strong men﴾. This divine report is evidence of the great wealth that the tyrant Qarun possessed, such that its keys would weigh heavily upon a band (ʿusbah), that is, a group of men, even if they all carried them, because of their weight. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿When his people said to him﴾, that is, the Israelites, admonishing and reminding him, ﴿Do not exult﴾, that is, over your wealth, with the exultation of the insolent and the haughty, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not like the exultant﴾, that is, the insolent and haughty who strut, boast and act proudly. ﴿And seek﴾, that is, seek ﴿through what Allah has given you﴾ of wealth ﴿the Abode of the Hereafter﴾, by giving charity from it and spending in the way of Allah, such as building a mosque, a school, an orphanage, a shelter, or other forms of righteousness and kindness. ﴿And do not forget your share of the world﴾, so eat, drink, dress, ride and dwell, but without extravagance or arrogance. ﴿And do good﴾ in the worship and obedience of Allah the Exalted and do good to His servants by word and deed, ﴿as Allah has done good to you﴾, that is, as Allah the Exalted has done good to you. ﴿And seek not corruption in the land﴾ by abandoning the obligations and committing the prohibitions. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not like the corrupters﴾. Whoever Allah does not love, He hates, and whoever He hates, He punishes in this world and the Hereafter. After this admonition from his righteous people, the people of knowledge and insight, this tyrant Qarun rejected it with what Allah the Exalted reported of him in His saying in verse [78]: ﴿He said: I was given it only on knowledge I have with me﴾, that is, do not threaten me or frighten me with the removal of my wealth from me if I do not do good. For this wealth, ﴿I was given it﴾, that is, Allah gave it to me with knowledge of me that I deserve it, and therefore He gave me and increased my giving. Allah the Exalted answered him in his claim: ﴿Does he not know﴾, that is, does he say what he says of this false claim without knowing ﴿that Allah had destroyed before him generations that were greater than him in strength and greater in accumulation﴾, such as ʿAd, Thamud and the people of Ibrahim. For if abundance of wealth were evidence of Allah's love and His approval of its possessor, He would not have destroyed ʿAd, Thamud and the people of Nuh before him, though they were stronger, and had more wealth and men. And His saying the Exalted: ﴿And the criminals will not be asked about their sins﴾, that is, when a servant greatly commits crimes through shirk and disobedience, the word of punishment becomes binding upon him and the time of his punishment arrives, and he will not be asked about his sins; rather he will be seized suddenly, just as these criminals will enter the Fire without reckoning, so they will not be questioned nor called to account.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks, and they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾ [al-Rahman: 41], that is, they will be thrown into Hell, and it will be said to them: ﴿This is Hell, which the criminals used to deny﴾ [al-Rahman: 43].

Guidance of the verses:

1- Wealth and high position are a means of corrupting a person, except for those whom Allah the Mighty and Majestic has mercy upon, and they are few.

2- The exultation in wealth and authority is forbidden when it is exultation of insolence, pride, self-glorification, arrogance and vanity.

3- Among Allah's favours upon the community is that there exist within it scholars who advise, guide and direct.

4- It is part of prudence for a person to seek from wealth, standing and position the highest ranks in Paradise.

5- Eating of the good, drinking of the good, and dressing, riding and dwelling are permissible, without extravagance, vanity or arrogance.

6- Whoever is blessed with health, wealth and the might of rulership is afflicted with delusion, except those whom Allah has mercy upon.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 79–82:

Explanation of the words:

*Fi zinatihi* (in his adornment): i.e., the clothing of festivals and official occasions.

*Ya layta lana mithla ma utiya Qarun* (Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun was given): i.e., they wished that they had been given wealth and adornment like what Qarun was given.

*Innahu la-dhu hazzin azim* (Indeed, he is truly possessed of a great fortune): i.e., he is truly possessed of good fortune and portion, which Allah bestowed upon him in the book of decrees.

*Wa qala alladhina utu al-'ilm* (And those who had been given knowledge said): i.e., those who had been given religious knowledge, through knowing Allah, the Hereafter, and the causes of happiness and misery.

*Waylakum* (Woe to you): i.e., woe and destruction are upon you for your wishing for wealth and the glitter of this world.

*Thawab Allah khayrun liman amana wa 'amila salihan* (The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds): i.e., what is with Allah of reward for the believers who do righteous deeds, which is Paradise, is better than the perishing trash of this world.

*Wa la yulaqqaha illa al-sabirun* (But none receives it except the patient): i.e., none is granted success in uttering this statement, "The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds," except those who are patient in faith and piety.

*Fa-khasafna bihi wa-bidarihi al-ard* (So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home): i.e., We made the earth sink beneath him, and he and his home and everyone who was with him there, from among the people of transgression and crime, were swallowed up.

*Tamanna makanahu bil-ams* (Those who had wished to be in his place yesterday): i.e., those who said, "Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun was given." Here "place" means station, and what Qarun had of rule, adornment, wealth and rank.

*Wa-ka'anna Allah yabsutu* (And indeed, [it is as if] Allah extends provision): i.e., I wonder, knowing that Allah extends provision to whom He wills.

*Wa yaqdir* (and restricts it): i.e., narrows it.

*Wa-ka'annahu la yuflih al-kafirun* (And indeed, [it is as if] the disbelievers do not succeed): i.e., I wonder, knowing that the disbelievers do not succeed, meaning that they will not win salvation from the Fire or entry into the Gardens as the believers win.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the story of Qarun the transgressor. Allah says: ﴿So he went out before his people﴾, i.e., Qarun went out on a day of festival or occasion before his people, while they watched his procession, ﴿in his adornment﴾, the special clothing and mounts. Allah's words: ﴿Those who desired the life of this world said﴾, i.e., from the people of Moses, those who were enamored with the world and its glitter, from among the heedless of the Hereafter, and how many of them there are today, and before and after today, said what Allah reported about them: ﴿Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun was given﴾, they wished that they had the wealth and adornment that Qarun was given. ﴿Indeed, he is truly possessed of a great fortune﴾, i.e., of good fortune, portion and provision. ﴿And those who had been given knowledge said﴾, i.e., of the sacred religious knowledge, those who know the world and the Hereafter and the causes of happiness and misery in each of them, said what Allah reported about them in His saying: ﴿Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, i.e., woe to you, you are destroyed if you prefer this perishing over the everlasting. ﴿The reward of Allah﴾, which is Paradise, ﴿is better than this perishing glitter﴾ ﴿for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, and it necessarily entails that they abandon polytheism and sins. Allah's words: ﴿But none receives it﴾, i.e., this statement of speech: ﴿The reward of Allah is better for those who believe﴾ in their Lord ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ in their lives by performing obligatory and voluntary acts and abandoning what is forbidden and vile, i.e., none receives this statement ﴿except the patient﴾ among the people of faith and piety. They are the ones whom Allah inspires with it, so they say it, owing to the purity of their souls and the purification of their selves. Allah's words in verse [81]: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾. Allah reports that He made the earth swallow Qarun and his home as retribution for his disbelief, hypocrisy, transgression and arrogance.

Allah's words: ﴿And he had no company to help him against Allah﴾, i.e., no group ﴿to support him against Allah﴾ when Allah willed to forsake him by causing the earth to swallow him and his home and those in it of his oppressive and criminal helpers. ﴿Nor was he among those who could defend themselves﴾, i.e., he could not save himself from what befell him of the sinking into the depths of the earth, in which he continues to sink until the Day of Resurrection. Allah's words: ﴿And by morning those who had wished to be in his place yesterday began to say﴾: Allah reports about those who said, on the day Qarun went out before them in his adornment, "Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun was given," that when they witnessed the sinking that befell Qarun and his home, they said, ﴿And indeed, [it is as if] Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it﴾, i.e., we marvel, knowing that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it, i.e., upon whom He wills; expansion and restriction are all in Allah's hand. So what is wrong with us that we do not turn to Allah seeking His pleasure and do not wish for what we wished, when he has gone, not seen by eye nor touched by hand? ﴿Had Allah not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us. And indeed, [it is as if] the disbelievers do not succeed﴾, i.e., we also marvel, knowing that the disbelievers such as Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman do not succeed, i.e., the disbelievers do not win, neither by salvation from punishment nor by entry into the Gardens.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification that temptation reaches the hearts of materialists, the children of this world, more quickly, may Allah protect us.

2- Clarification of the position of the people of religious knowledge, that they are rushd, i.e., wise, who enjoin good and forbid evil.

3- Clarification that transgression is punished in this world for the transgressors and they are tormented for it in the Hereafter.

4- Clarification that the existence of faith is better than its absence, even if little, and that the possessor of faith is closer to repentance than one who has no faith.

The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, i.e., woe to you, you are destroyed if you prefer this perishing over the everlasting. ﴿The reward of Allah﴾, which is Paradise, ﴿is better than this perishing glitter﴾ ﴿for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, and it necessarily entails that they abandon polytheism and sins. Allah's words: ﴿But none receives it﴾, i.e., this statement of speech: ﴿The reward of Allah is better for those who believe﴾ in their Lord ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ in their lives by performing obligatory and voluntary acts and abandoning what is forbidden and vile, i.e., none receives this statement ﴿except the patient﴾ among the people of faith and piety. They are the ones whom Allah inspires with it, so they say it, owing to the purity of their souls and the purification of their selves. Allah's words in verse [81]: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾. Allah reports that He made the earth swallow Qarun and his home as retribution for his disbelief, hypocrisy, transgression and arrogance.

Allah's words: ﴿And he had no company to help him against Allah﴾, i.e., no group ﴿to support him against Allah﴾ when Allah willed to forsake him by causing the earth to swallow him and his home and those in it of his oppressive and criminal helpers. ﴿Nor was he among those who could defend themselves﴾, i.e., he could not save himself from what befell him of the sinking into the depths of the earth, in which he continues to sink until the Day of Resurrection. Allah's words: ﴿And by morning those who had wished to be in his place yesterday began to say﴾: Allah reports about those who said, on the day Qarun went out before them in his adornment, "Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun was given," that when they witnessed the sinking that befell Qarun and his home, they said, ﴿And indeed, [it is as if] Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it﴾, i.e., we marvel, knowing that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it, i.e., upon whom He wills; expansion and restriction are all in Allah's hand. And indeed, [it is as if] the disbelievers do not succeed﴾, i.e., we also marvel, knowing that the disbelievers such as Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman do not succeed, i.e., the disbelievers do not win, neither by salvation from punishment nor by entry into the Gardens.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification that temptation reaches the hearts of materialists, the children of this world, more quickly, may Allah protect us.

2- Clarification of the position of the people of religious knowledge, that they are rushd, i.e., wise, who enjoin good and forbid evil.

3- Clarification that transgression is punished in this world for the transgressors and they are tormented for it in the Hereafter.

4- Clarification that the existence of faith is better than its absence, even if little, and that the possessor of faith is closer to repentance than one who has no faith.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verse 83–84:

Explanation of the words:

"Tilka al-dar al-akhirah" (That is the Final Abode): that is Paradise, the abode of the righteous (al-abrar).

"La yuridun 'uluwwan fi al-ard" (They do not desire haughtiness on earth): that is, tyranny (baghy) and no domineering over people.

"Wa la fasadan" (Nor corruption): that is, they do not desire corruption by committing acts of disobedience.

"Wa al-'aqibah" (And the good outcome): that is, the praiseworthy end in this world and the Hereafter.

"Lil-muttaqin" (For the God-conscious): those who guard themselves against what displeases God, so they do not believe, say, or do what God, exalted is He, does not approve of.

"Man ja'a bil-hasanah" (Whoever comes with a good deed): that is, on the Day of Resurrection. The good deed (hasanah) is the fruit of obedience to God, exalted is He, for which the believer is rewarded.

"Fa-lahu khayrun minha" (Then he will have better than it): that is, it will be multiplied for him tenfold.

"Wa man ja'a bil-sayyi'ah" (And whoever comes with an evil deed): the evil deed (sayyi'ah) is the fruit of disobedience to God, for which the servant is punished if God, exalted is He, does not pardon him.

Meaning of the verses:

It has already preceded in the context that the reward of God, which is Paradise, is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds. So He, exalted is He, pointed to it with His saying, ﴿That is the Final Abode﴾, which is Paradise, since it is the last abode that the God-conscious dwell in, and they do not leave it. "We shall make it" is the predicate of His saying "That is the Final Abode." So He, exalted is He, informs that He makes it a place of refuge and dwelling for those who do not desire haughtiness on earth nor corruption: they do not desire domineering over people, self-exaltation, arrogance toward them, or tyranny. And not corruption by committing acts of disobedience such as murder, adultery, theft, and drinking wine. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And the good outcome is for the God-conscious﴾, means: the praiseworthy outcome in both abodes belongs to the people of faith and God-consciousness, who are the believers who guard themselves against what displeases God, mighty and majestic is He, by performing what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden. His saying, ﴿Whoever comes﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿with a good deed﴾, which is obedience to God and His Messenger, ﴿then he will have﴾ the reward of the multiplication of the good deed by ten times its like, and it may be multiplied to more, on condition that it is not a good deed given to him from the good deeds of a wrongdoer in this world; such a deed is not multiplied. For the good deed that he himself performed is what is multiplied, just as the good deed of one who intended a good deed but did not do it is not multiplied, since he did not actually perform it, though it is recorded for him as a good deed. His saying, ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection. The evil deed is the fruit of disobedience to God and His Messenger in one's self, ﴿then he will not be recompensed﴾ except with its like, that is, it is not multiplied against him; this is because of God's justice and His compassion toward His servants. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except for what they used to do﴾, namely of shirk and sins, ﴿except for what they used to do﴾, that is, in this world, since it is the abode of action, and the Hereafter is the abode of recompense.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The prohibition of arrogance and of domineering over people, and of acting on sins, and that this is corruption on earth.

2- Clarification of God's favor, mercy, and justice among His servants through the multiplication of good deeds and the non-multiplication of evil deeds.

3- The good outcome, which is Paradise, belongs to the people of faith and God-consciousness.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 85–88:

Explanation of the words:

Inna alladhi faraḍa ʿalayka al-Qur'an: i.e., God, who sent down the Qur'an to you, made its recitation obligatory upon you, and made obligatory its practice and its conveyance (to people).

La-rādduka ilā maʿād: i.e., to return you to Makkah as a conqueror, for the maʿād (place of return) of a man is the land to which he returns (maʿād, lit. "return", here a place of return).

Wa-mā kunta tarjū: i.e., you did not expect or hope that the Qur'an would be sent down to you and revealed to you.

Illā raḥmatan min rabbika: but by a mercy from your Lord and a bounty He sent down to you.

Fa-lā takūnanna ẓahīran: i.e., among the thanks for this blessing is that you should not be a helper to the disbelievers.

Wa-lā yaṣuddannaka: i.e., let them not divert you from acting upon God's signs after God has honoured you by sending them down to you.

Wa-udʿu ilā rabbika: i.e., call people to belief in God, to worshipping Him, and to abandoning association (shirk) with Him.

Wa-lā tadʿu maʿa Allāhi ilāhan ākhar: i.e., do not worship another god alongside God by calling upon it, sacrificing to it, or vowing to it.

Kullu shayʾin hālik: i.e., perishing.

Illā wajhahu: i.e., except God, glorified and exalted is He, who does not perish as everything else perishes.

Explanation of the meanings of the verses:

The noble context has previously called to the three foundations of religion: tawhid (the oneness of God), prophethood, and resurrection and recompense. This is the conclusion of that in this noble surah. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, He who ordained for you the Qur'an will surely bring you back to a place of return﴾, i.e., He sent it down to you, made its recitation obligatory upon you, its conveyance, and its practice. ﴿will surely bring you back﴾, i.e., to your return ﴿to a place of return﴾, which is the return to Makkah after your departure from it and your longing to return to it, and to Paradise after your death, since you entered it on the night you were taken up to the heavens. In this is an affirmation of his prophethood ﷺ through revelation to him. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance and who is in clear error"﴾ is a teaching to him ﷺ of how to respond to the polytheists who accused him of being astray in his call and of departing from the religion of his fathers and forefathers. He was taught to say to them: "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance, and that is me, the Messenger of God, and who is in clear error, and that is you, O polytheists." And His saying ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be sent down to you﴾, i.e., and you, O Muhammad, did not hope that the Qur'an would be sent down to you, and that was before his ﷺ prophethood. And His saying ﴿but it was a mercy from your Lord﴾, i.e., but the mercy of your Lord upon you required its sending down to you, so that you would be the Messenger of God to all the worlds. This is a great blessing and a mighty favour, so give thanks for it by the following:

(1) ﴿So never be a supporter of the disbelievers﴾, i.e., a helper to them in any circumstance.

(2) ﴿And let them not divert you from the signs of God after they have been sent down to you﴾, so that you abandon their recitation, their conveyance, and acting upon them. In this is an affirmation of Muhammadan prophethood.

(3) ﴿And call to your Lord﴾: call people to the oneness of your Lord and to acting upon His law.

(4) ﴿And never be among the polytheists﴾, i.e., disassociate yourself from them, do not be content with their shirk, and call them to its opposite, which is tawhid.

(5) ﴿And do not call upon another god besides God﴾, i.e., do not worship another god alongside God, neither by supplication, nor by vows and sacrifice, nor by offering any offering or obedience to other than God, glorified and exalted is He. In this is an affirmation of tawhid. And His saying ﴿There is no god but Him﴾ is an affirmation of tawhid by negating that there be any god with God.

And His saying ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾ informs that every deed not done for the sake of God's Face is void and gone, with no reward for it. Likewise, everything other than God, mighty and majestic is He, perishes, and only God, glorified and exalted is He, remains, as in His saying: ﴿Everything upon it will perish, and there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honour﴾ [al-Rahman: 26–27]. ﴿To Him belongs the judgment﴾, i.e., the just decision among His servants. And His saying ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾, i.e., after death, for reckoning and recompense on the day of your resurrection and gathering to Him, mighty and majestic is He. In this is an affirmation of resurrection and recompense. And all praise is due to God, first and last.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The miracle of the Qur'an in the occurrence of the unseen after it was foretold, namely that the Messenger ﷺ returned to Makkah after having left it.

2- The permissibility of gentleness in debate and argument during da'wah, by using the method of raising doubts.

3- The prohibition of aiding and supporting the disbelievers, especially against the believers.

4- The obligation of steadfastness and patience in da'wah until its success through conveying it to people and their responding to it.

5- The affirmation of tawhid, resurrection, and Muhammadan prophethood.

6- The perishing of everything except God, Exalted, except what evidence has established will not perish. Eight such things are counted, which one of them arranged in verse: "They are the Throne, the Footstool, the Fire, and Paradise, / And 'Ajb (the coccyx), and spirits, likewise the Tablet and the Pen."

Likewise, everything other than God, mighty and majestic is He, perishes, and only God, glorified and exalted is He, remains, as in His saying: ﴿Everything upon it will perish, and there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honour﴾ [al-Rahman: 26–27]. ﴿To Him belongs the judgment﴾, i.e., the just decision among His servants. In this is an affirmation of resurrection and recompense. And all praise is due to God, first and last.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The miracle of the Qur'an in the occurrence of the unseen after it was foretold, namely that the Messenger ﷺ returned to Makkah after having left it.

2- The permissibility of gentleness in debate and argument during da'wah, by using the method of raising doubts.

3- The prohibition of aiding and supporting the disbelievers, especially against the believers.

4- The obligation of steadfastness and patience in da'wah until its success through conveying it to people and their responding to it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 28, verses 85–88:

Explanation of the words:

Inna alladhi faraḍa ʿalayka al-Qur'an: i.e., God, who sent down the Qur'an to you, made its recitation obligatory upon you, and made obligatory its practice and its conveyance (to people).

La-rādduka ilā maʿād: i.e., to return you to Makkah as a conqueror, for the maʿād (place of return) of a man is the land to which he returns (maʿād, lit. "return", here a place of return).

Wa-mā kunta tarjū: i.e., you did not expect or hope that the Qur'an would be sent down to you and revealed to you.

Illā raḥmatan min rabbika: but by a mercy from your Lord and a bounty He sent down to you.

Fa-lā takūnanna ẓahīran: i.e., among the thanks for this blessing is that you should not be a helper to the disbelievers.

Wa-lā yaṣuddannaka: i.e., let them not divert you from acting upon God's signs after God has honoured you by sending them down to you.

Wa-udʿu ilā rabbika: i.e., call people to belief in God, to worshipping Him, and to abandoning association (shirk) with Him.

Wa-lā tadʿu maʿa Allāhi ilāhan ākhar: i.e., do not worship another god alongside God by calling upon it, sacrificing to it, or vowing to it.

Kullu shayʾin hālik: i.e., perishing.

Illā wajhahu: i.e., except God, glorified and exalted is He, who does not perish as everything else perishes.

Explanation of the meanings of the verses:

The noble context has previously called to the three foundations of religion: tawhid (the oneness of God), prophethood, and resurrection and recompense. This is the conclusion of that in this noble surah. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, He who ordained for you the Qur'an will surely bring you back to a place of return﴾, i.e., He sent it down to you, made its recitation obligatory upon you, its conveyance, and its practice. ﴿will surely bring you back﴾, i.e., to your return ﴿to a place of return﴾, which is the return to Makkah after your departure from it and your longing to return to it, and to Paradise after your death, since you entered it on the night you were taken up to the heavens. In this is an affirmation of his prophethood ﷺ through revelation to him. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance and who is in clear error"﴾ is a teaching to him ﷺ of how to respond to the polytheists who accused him of being astray in his call and of departing from the religion of his fathers and forefathers. He was taught to say to them: "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance, and that is me, the Messenger of God, and who is in clear error, and that is you, O polytheists." And His saying ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be sent down to you﴾, i.e., and you, O Muhammad, did not hope that the Qur'an would be sent down to you, and that was before his ﷺ prophethood. And His saying ﴿but it was a mercy from your Lord﴾, i.e., but the mercy of your Lord upon you required its sending down to you, so that you would be the Messenger of God to all the worlds. This is a great blessing and a mighty favour, so give thanks for it by the following:

(1) ﴿So never be a supporter of the disbelievers﴾, i.e., a helper to them in any circumstance.

(2) ﴿And let them not divert you from the signs of God after they have been sent down to you﴾, so that you abandon their recitation, their conveyance, and acting upon them. In this is an affirmation of Muhammadan prophethood.

(3) ﴿And call to your Lord﴾: call people to the oneness of your Lord and to acting upon His law.

(4) ﴿And never be among the polytheists﴾, i.e., disassociate yourself from them, do not be content with their shirk, and call them to its opposite, which is tawhid.

(5) ﴿And do not call upon another god besides God﴾, i.e., do not worship another god alongside God, neither by supplication, nor by vows and sacrifice, nor by offering any offering or obedience to other than God, glorified and exalted is He. In this is an affirmation of tawhid. And His saying ﴿There is no god but Him﴾ is an affirmation of tawhid by negating that there be any god with God.

And His saying ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾ informs that every deed not done for the sake of God's Face is void and gone, with no reward for it. Likewise, everything other than God, mighty and majestic is He, perishes, and only God, glorified and exalted is He, remains, as in His saying: ﴿Everything upon it will perish, and there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honour﴾ [al-Rahman: 26–27]. ﴿To Him belongs the judgment﴾, i.e., the just decision among His servants. And His saying ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾, i.e., after death, for reckoning and recompense on the day of your resurrection and gathering to Him, mighty and majestic is He. In this is an affirmation of resurrection and recompense. And all praise is due to God, first and last.
